name: ACCEL Middle College (East Side Union / Evergreen Valley College)

name: Youth Innovation Program (WIOA In-School Youth)

name: Alameda County Youth Innovation Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Services include paid and unpaid work experience, so ask the provider about pay.
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 who are currently in high school or college. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use a separate county youth program.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the program page: Eden ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. County line: 510-259-3842.
notes: Two providers only: Eden ROP (Hayward) and Tri-Valley ROP (Livermore), so which one serves you depends on where you live. Pay is not stated. A Hayward AJCC fact sheet (Rubicon Programs) mentions federal WIOA youth ages 14 to 24 with at least one barrier; ask your provider about younger teens. See also Youth Innovation Program (WIOA In-School Youth), a separate listing from the same county board that names the same two providers.

name: After School Matters (paid apprenticeships and assistantships)
pay_detail: Paid stipend based on program level and frequency. Dollar amounts vary by program and are not stated on the apply page.
duration: Spring: late Feb to mid May. Summer: late June to early Aug. Fall 2026: Sept 28 to Dec 12.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 application opened Aug 26 and programs started Sept 28; no closing date stated and spaces are limited. Spring 2027 applications open in January; summer 2027 in April (per the session timeline).
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Most programs are ages 14 to 18 (14 by Sept 28, 2026 for the fall session). Outreach Assistantships need age 16+.
how_to_apply: Apply online (up to six programs, ranked). Save your Application ID for the Teen Dashboard. Most programs require an interview; offers must be accepted within 72 hours. A parent/guardian consent form is required after you accept.
notes: One program per session. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required for every program; teens without one should contact ASM. Applying again each session needs a new application. The fall page says the application is open, but programs began Sept 28, so confirm spots remain. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.

name: California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of California
city: California (session location not stated on the site)
grades: 11th grade (the site says each delegate is an 11th grader during the 2025-26 school year)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the pages read. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22-27, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 22-27, 2026. 2027 dates and application deadlines are not posted on the site.

how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit (the site has a spreadsheet to find one). Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Students at schools with no sponsoring Unit can use the START HERE online application as Department alternate applicants.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages read.

name: Alameda County Community Food Bank: Volunteer
duration: Shifts

notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.

notes: The teen page is thin. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

name: Alameda Youth Career and Job Fair

name: Palefsky Collision Project (Alliance Theatre)

notes: Free thanks to the Palefsky family. Exact dates were not printed on the application page, only the January to mid-April range. The Alliance also lists a year-long Teen Ensemble, but its current page was not read so it is not listed.

name: VolunTEENS at the Aquarium of the Pacific
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program (60 service hours).

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 16. Applicants complete an online application and an on-site interview, then required trainings. Both a parent and the teen sign liability forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during an open window, attend an interview, then the online and on-site training days.
notes: Spring and Fall sessions are weekends only; Summer shifts run seven days a week. The Aquarium also lists other youth roles for ages 11 to 18 (Ocean Neighbors, Teen Science Cafe Volunteer, Student Eco-Ambassadors). The Education Volunteer role is for ages 16 and up with at least 100 hours in six months.

In-school or out-of-school youth who face a barrier such as offender history, homelessness, foster care, parenting, disability or being a basic-skills-deficient or English learner diploma holder.

Gwinnett: 404-913-0769 (3805 Crestwood Pkwy NW, Suite 300, Duluth). Cherokee: 770-345-5483. Henry: 404-913-0769. Douglas: 770-997-4511. Fayette: 770-910-7733. Rockdale: 770-991-7608.

name: TRIO Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math and Science (American River College)

how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read, so ask staff for current dates.

name: SPEAK Student Volunteers (Atlanta Botanical Garden)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: 50 hours between June 2 and July 24 (2026), including a required 6-hour training day. Shifts Tuesday to Sunday in 2-hour blocks.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: info sessions Jan 13 and Feb 10, application and recommendation due March 1, 2026, group interviews March 21 or 28. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older by June 2 of the summer.
how_to_apply: Submit the online SPEAK application and have a non-relative adult submit a recommendation form. Attend a 2-hour group interview and the mandatory training day. If you also apply to the paid internship, only the internship application is needed.
notes: Application window usually closes March 1 (2026 pattern). Check the Garden volunteer page in December and January for the 2027 cycle.

name: Summer High School Internship (Atlanta Botanical Garden)
pay_detail: $12 per hour, paid every two weeks.
duration: 7 weeks (June 2 to July 16 in 2026), 18 hours a week, Tuesday through Thursday
deadline_text: The Garden says to check back in December 2026 for Summer 2027 details.
who_can_apply: 16 or older by June 2 of the summer, and a rising sophomore, junior or senior at a Metro Atlanta Title I school. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the internship application and have a non-relative adult (teacher, mentor or boss) submit the recommendation form. Group interview at the Garden, then virtual orientation with a guardian. Questions: lboren@atlantabg.org.
notes: Only for students at Metro Atlanta Title I schools. Work is outside in all weather and includes lifting 40 lbs. Applying here also covers the SPEAK volunteer program. The Garden's Gainesville site has its own separate teen program.

name: Atlanta Teen Leader Program and Parks and Recreation Teen Summer Employment
org: City of Atlanta, Department of Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Teen Leader activities are free. Pay for the summer employment program is not stated in the catalog.
duration: The 2026 Teen Leaders Summer Academy ran June 8 to July 24, Monday to Friday.
deadline_text: Register as a Teen Leader by Dec 31, 2026 to be considered for the Parks and Recreation summer employment program. That date is a registration cutoff, not a job application. Registration is ongoing. The catalog says summer 2026 employment registration is closed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Participating sites listed: Adams, Bessie Branham, C. T. Martin, Dunbar, Grove Park, Martin Luther King Jr., Peachtree Hills, Pittman, Rosel Fann, Thomasville, William Walker, Zaban, @Promise South and @Promise MLK. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register for the Atlanta Teen Leader Program. The catalog lists atlantaga.gov/iparcs as the City registration site for its programs. Confirm the steps with your nearest participating recreation center.
notes: Source is the City's 2026 summer catalog, so it does not say which summer the Dec 31, 2026 cutoff is for (most likely summer 2027). Ages and pay for the actual summer jobs are not stated. Georgia requires a work permit for any job under 16. The City's iParcs page blocked automated reading.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Atlanta, Department of Labor and Employment Services
pay_detail: Paid. The page says competitive wages and does not state a rate.
duration: June 8 to July 16 in 2026 (about 6 weeks). Some positions may extend.
deadline_text: The 2026 program ran in June and July. Registration was a waiting list when we read the page. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Atlanta youth ages 14 to 24. Documents asked for: original birth certificate, proof of City of Atlanta residency, state or school photo ID, original Social Security card, and a work permit for anyone under 16.
how_to_apply: Register online on the city's SYEP sign-up page with an email address you check daily. Upload your documents in the SYEP portal when asked. You are matched to openings, invited to orientation, and sent an offer letter. Some employers interview first.
notes: A work permit is needed only for ages 14 and 15 (Georgia requires one under 16). You start it after you have a job offer, through your school district. Not guaranteed: the city says selection is competitive. Questions: syep@atlantaga.gov or (404) 546-3000. The registration list asks for an original Social Security card; this is the official city program, so upload documents only inside the SYEP portal and never send them by email or text. The city's atlantaga.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm the 2027 timeline with the SYEP team.

name: BART Summer Internship (high school)

notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.

notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.

duration: Winter 2027 placements run January to March 2027

notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.

name: Beyond Emancipation (B:E) employment coaching for foster youth

how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The program page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.
who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by park
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.
who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.
duration: Club year
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.
who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.
who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. Age and grade rules were not on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages I read.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Counted as school credit.
duration: 3 years
deadline_text: Application is through the school that hosts the academy.
who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy sets its own application. Search the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy, or check nearby high schools. Whether students from other districts may transfer in depends on the district's open enrollment rules.
notes: The CDE site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (bot check), so this card could not be re-confirmed against the official page. Grades 10 to 12 and the school-within-a-school model need confirming. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

name: Supporting Student Success (WIOA In-School Youth)
org: Contra Costa County Office of Education
city: Contra Costa County, CA (West County and East County)
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Ongoing
who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.

name: Cedars-Sinai Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers buy the required volunteer jacket for $30 (cash) and wear black or white scrubs.
duration: Winter/Spring and Fall: one 2-hour shift a week for 10 weeks (20 hours). Summer: two 4-hour shifts a week for 5 weeks (40 hours).
deadline_text: 2027 sessions: Winter/Spring (Jan 25 to Apr 4) applications Nov 23, 2026; Summer (Jun 21 to Jul 25) applications Mar 29, 2027; Fall (Oct 4 to Dec 12) applications Aug 2, 2027. First come, first served; each application closes when spots fill.
who_can_apply: Students 14 to 18 enrolled in high school with a transcript showing at least a 3.2 GPA. New volunteers and one parent or guardian must attend a mandatory in-person Teen Information Session.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with your transcript, finish the online volunteer orientation, complete health screening and flu vaccine (flu season Nov 1 to Apr 30), and attend the Teen Information Session (Monday, Jan 11, 2027, 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.).
notes: Spots are limited and fill fast, so apply the day the window opens. Shifts run Monday to Sunday. Teens who want research should look at Cedars-Sinai's separate INSPIRE Internship Program (not checked here). Questions: TeenVolunteerProgram@cshs.org or 310-423-8044.

name: Chabot College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, complete the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: cc-earlycollege@chabotcollege.edu or 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.

name: Galaxy Explorers Program
grades: Typically enters the summer before 10th grade and stays through 12th grade
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
deadline_text: Applications open each year from February 1 to March 31. Decisions in early May, orientation early to mid June. The page does not list 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated, so needs_work_permit is null.

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
pay_detail: The program page does not state pay. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around a stipend.
duration: Spring, fall and winter: 8 weeks, 6 hours a week. Summer: 6 weeks, 30 program days.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who live in Chicago.
how_to_apply: Contact the staff at the park you are interested in to start the application. The process is an application, an interview, a mentoring curriculum and performance check-ins.
notes: The page says RIT is a job readiness program and participants are not Park District staff. The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older for lifeguards, recreation leaders, special recreation leaders and junior laborers. The page does not state a residency rule, so check with the Park District.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Park District job site from the Learn More and Apply Now links on the Summer Jobs page, or at a Teen Opportunity Fair. Applications must be in by the closed date on each job posting.
notes: Work permit: Illinois requires employment certificates only for minors under 16 (Illinois Dept. of Labor FAQ). All of these jobs start at 16. Teens 13 to 15 should see the Recreation Leader in Training program. Fair email: teensinthepark@chicagoparkdistrict.com.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.
who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 and 15 who live in Chicago. At least half of participants come from priority groups (for example youth with disabilities, English learners, youth in foster care or experiencing homelessness).
how_to_apply: Apply through the online Chicago Youth Works application. Youth under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form if offered a position. Partner agencies contact applicants directly.
notes: The Chicago Youth Works FAQ says youth under 16 may be required to have a work permit; Illinois law requires one for most under-16 jobs, issued through the school district or ISBE. Ask the program whether a stipend program needs one. The FAQ says the Chicago Housing Authority, After School Matters and DFSS each also have a limited number of slots for 14 and 15 year olds.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21.

name: FARMS Leadership Program
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.
duration: school year, 6+ field days
deadline_text: No dates posted. Schools sign up as groups.
who_can_apply: High school students at participating schools in 14 counties, including Sacramento and Yolo. Ask the FARMS coordinator at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag or science teacher whether your school participates. Contact Mindy Cunha at mindy@landbasedlearning.org.
notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.

name: Urban Ag Internships
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.
duration: year-long
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Students at Luther Burbank High, Grant Union High and Sacramento Academic and Vocational Academy (SAVA).
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Ask a teacher or counselor at your host school, or contact the Center for Land-Based Learning: info@landbasedlearning.org or (530) 795-1520.
notes: Only at the three host schools. Grant Union students can earn college credit through a Sacramento State partnership (ACE program). Pay rate and hours per week are not posted. Paid job for a minor, so a work permit is likely needed.

name: CTAE Work-Based Learning, Cobb County School District
pay_detail: Placements may be paid or non-paid, according to the district page.
duration: A school year; students can be in WBL both junior and senior year. A 90-minute block needs at least 7.5 work hours a week.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Ask your school's coordinator for the application window.
who_can_apply: Cobb County School District juniors and seniors who are 16 or older. Your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator gives school-specific rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. All applications must be completed in full before they are considered. The district page lists a coordinator for each high school.
notes: District CTAE and WBL coordinator on the page: Sapph Espinoza. The job should relate to your career goals and CTAE coursework. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: B.O.S.S. Young Professionals Program (CobbWorks)
org: CobbWorks (Cobb County workforce board, WorkSource Cobb)
pay_detail: Participants can earn up to $8,500 across the program's activities, according to the program page.
duration: Not stated. Participants enter at any stage.
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Cobb County residents ages 16 to 24 who meet income qualifications (decided at eligibility) and are in one of the program's target groups.
how_to_apply: Fill out the B.O.S.S. application inquiry form online (it asks if you live in Cobb County, are 16 to 24, and are in school), or call 770-528-4300 or email bossinfo@cobbworks.org.
notes: Funded through WIOA, so participants must meet eligibility rules. The same site lists a PowerUp! plumbing pre-apprenticeship and a Cobb County Fire P.R.E.P. Academy for young adults; ages are not stated, so ask CobbWorks. The main cobbworks.org site returned an error, so this entry uses worksourcecobb.org. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: College of San Mateo Dual Enrollment and Concurrent Enrollment
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.
deadline_text: No application deadline stated on the pages read.
who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: high school students in grades 9 to 12. Dual enrollment: students at CSM's partner high schools; talk to your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Create an OpenCCC account and apply to CSM online. For dual enrollment, meet with your high school counselor first, then register with the Dual Enrollment team. Questions: csmoutreach@smccd.edu.
notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).

name: Computer History Museum Teen Volunteer Intern Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: Applications are currently closed. Join the interest list to hear about the next round.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the CHM internships page to join the mailing list.
notes: CHM says it is not accepting Teen Program applications right now; the page gives no reopening date. Join the interest list to be told when it opens. Pay and length are not stated.

name: Congressional App Challenge
pay_detail: Free
duration: Build time before the deadline
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline for registering and submitting is October 26, 2026.
who_can_apply: Middle or high school students living in the US (citizenship not required). Solo or teams up to four. Half the team must live in the district.
how_to_apply: Register on the Student Registration page, then submit the app online.
notes: Any language or platform is allowed, solo or teams up to four. Check the Participating Districts page on the site to confirm your district takes part.

name: Contra Costa College Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: Free: no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
who_can_apply: Students at West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies, or Middle College High School on campus. Requirements vary by school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: earlycollegecredit@contracosta.edu.
notes: Serves West Contra Costa County (Richmond, San Pablo). No deadlines are listed on the page.

name: Contra Costa County Library Teen Volunteers
city: Contra Costa County, CA (Richmond, Concord, Pleasant Hill and other branches)
grades: Entering 8th grade or above (Summer Read); age 16+ for other roles
duration: Summer Read 1 to 2 hours a week; Computer Docents at least 2 hours a week
deadline_text: Summer Read recruiting starts in April. Some libraries take volunteers on a limited basis.
who_can_apply: Summer Read: entering 8th grade or above, with parent consent. Computer Docent and Homework Help: age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer interest form on ccclib.org/volunteer. You may be called for an interview. Forms stay on file for six months.
notes: Contact your branch to see if it is taking volunteers now.

name: COSMOS (California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science) at UC Davis
pay_detail: Program cost $5,793 (2027 page), plus $48 application fee and a 2.5% card fee. Financial aid is available for admitted students with need, but not guaranteed.
duration: about 4 weeks (2027 dates TBA)
deadline_text: Application opens Jan 6, 2027 at 8:00 AM and closes Feb 5, 2027 (dates page says 5:00 PM). Financial aid forms postmarked by Feb 6, 2027. Decisions Mar 25, 2027.
who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Non-California residents and international students cannot apply. Selected on academic strength and interest in math and science. You pick one campus and cluster choices.
how_to_apply: Online application plus teacher recommendations and parent signature. Pay the application fee. If accepted, pay one-third by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027.
notes: Competitive. Residential, so you live on campus for four weeks. Financial aid is reviewed separately from admission and needs a parent income document; it has a hard deadline. Program session dates are listed as TBA. Pick UC Davis as your campus on the application. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz); this card is the Davis campus. See the UC COSMOS site for the others: https://jacobs.ucsd.edu/cosmos

name: Costa Mesa Parks and Community Services part-time jobs
pay_detail: The page says all positions start at $20 an hour. The page was last updated May 11, 2023, so confirm the rate.
duration: Part time, 8 to 30 hours a week
deadline_text: Jobs are posted on the city's job page. No dates are stated.
who_can_apply: The page does not state a minimum age. Ask the department before you apply, because lifeguard jobs and leader jobs often have different age rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the city's Parks and Community Services employment page.
notes: The city also runs free after-school teen centers for grades 7 to 12 and a Summer Teen Camp for grades 7 to 10, which are programs to attend, not jobs.

name: Teen Action Academy and Teen Leadership Committee
deadline_text: Not posted on the volunteer page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (two separate groups).
how_to_apply: No steps are posted. Email MadisonLeeRosen@CosumnesCSD.gov, call the District at 916-405-5600, or fill out the General Volunteer Interest Form on cosumnescsd.gov.
notes: Meeting times, location and deadlines are not posted on the page, so ask the District. Other volunteer roles on that page (adaptive recreation, youth coaching) are 18 and older.

name: Cosumnes Fire Department Explorer Program
org: Cosumnes Community Services District Fire Department
duration: School year
deadline_text: Applications for the next school year open in Spring 2027 (no exact date or closing date posted).
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, high school juniors and seniors, 2.0 GPA, and a physician-completed medical exam form.
how_to_apply: Email explorers@cosumnescsd.gov to get application details. Fire Admin phone: 916-405-7100.
notes: Serves the Elk Grove area. Needs a physician-completed medical exam form. Meeting schedule and any costs are not posted on the page.

name: Chicago Public Library paid summer teen internships
org: Chicago Public Library with After School Matters
pay_detail: 2026: $17.05 per hour, 20 hours a week
duration: 6 weeks (June 22 to Aug 1 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 posting says applications are closed. 2027 dates not posted; the Chicago Youth Works summer application ran March 10 to May 29 in 2026.
who_can_apply: Chicago residents attending a Chicago high school or equivalent (graduating seniors can apply), ages 16 to 19 on the first day (June 22 in 2026), with a Social Security number or ITIN.
how_to_apply: Log in to Chicago Youth Works, finish that application, choose After School Matters under Opportunities, then search library positions (program name CPL or your branch) in the ASM application. Branch staff interview in May.
notes: Positions were offered at every Chicago Public Library location. You can apply to many branches but be hired for one. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age here is 16. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org.

name: Chicago Public Library teen assistantships (Teen Best Reads, Teen Gamer's Guild, Teen Media Lab)
org: Chicago Public Library with After School Matters
pay_detail: These are stipend assistantships. The amounts are not stated on the page we read, so check the library's page.
duration: Starts Jan 9, 2027. Gamer's Guild to June 10; Media Lab Jan to June 22 and Sept 7 to Dec 14; Best Reads to Dec 14.
deadline_text: Applications open Monday Oct 19, 2026 and close Sunday Nov 8, 2026.
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Ages 14 to 19 on the start date of Jan 9, 2027. Teen Best Reads and Teen Media Lab are open to current 9th, 10th and 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Chicago Public Library application form (not the After School Matters site). Answer the open-ended questions carefully; they decide who is interviewed. Virtual interview in Microsoft Teams for each program. Apply to as many as you like but accept one.
notes: You enroll with After School Matters during the first month, which needs a Social Security Number and parent or guardian information. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org. Gamer's Guild sub-guilds meet at different library branches.

name: CPMC Information Desk Volunteer (Van Ness Campus, Sutter Health)
org: Sutter Health, California Pacific Medical Center (CPMC)
city: San Francisco, CA (CPMC Van Ness Campus, 1101 Van Ness Avenue)
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the listing
duration: Minimum 100 hours in one year, at least three to four hours per week
deadline_text: The listing shows Actively Recruiting. No application deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older. Some departments accept only people 18 and older. Junior volunteers under 18 need a signed parental consent form.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, then an in-person interview and a health screening. The background check applies to adults only. Questions go to cpmcvolunteer@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing 2026-10-07. Not stated on the listing: TB test or immunization requirements, application window, and pay (unpaid volunteer role). The health screening is required but its contents are not described on this listing. Sutter's separate CPMC student volunteer page could not be read from this environment, so no details from it are used here. The listing is a lobby role, so it fits teens 16 and older who want to try hospital volunteering; it is not a high school program.

name: CPS Career and Technical Education (CTE) pathways
fields: tech-cs; health; trades; business-finance; food-hospitality; arts-media; education; law-government; engineering; environment
duration: Multi-year pathway
deadline_text: GoCPS high school application dates are not stated on the CTE page; check GoCPS.
who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students. 8th graders apply through GoCPS when they apply to high school; freshmen and 10th graders ask their school counselor.
how_to_apply: Rank CTE programs on your GoCPS high school application (8th grade), or talk to your counselor (9th and 10th grade). Email CTE@cps.edu for questions.
notes: Which pathways are offered differs by school; the CTE Matrix and Guide to CTE Programs on the page list them. CPS Work-Based Learning (internships, co-op) builds on these pathways. Contact: 773-553-2108.

name: Chicago Builds (CPS construction pre-apprenticeship)
pay_detail: Earn 2.5 high school credits per year of the program. Pay for senior-year internships is not stated.
duration: Two school years, 2 hours a day at Dunbar High School campus (3000 S. King Drive)
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed April 17, 2026 (decisions by May 22). 2027-28 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Current 10th and 11th graders at a district-run CPS school; priority goes to 10th graders. Must attend an information session and submit a recommendation from a trusted adult who is not a family member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google application form, a signed Student and Parent Expectations and Consent Contract and a Recommendation Form, then email everything to ChicagoBuilds@cps.edu.
notes: It is an Illinois Works Pre-Apprenticeship site and offers the Master Builder program with City Colleges of Chicago. Classes meet during the school day in an AM or PM cohort. Contact: 773-534-0909.

name: CPS Cooperative Education (senior-year work study)
pay_detail: Students earn wages; the rate is not stated on the page.
duration: One school year, at least 180 hours a semester (about 10 hours a week); 3 elective credits
deadline_text: Students must apply during junior year. Application dates not stated on the page.
who_can_apply: High school seniors at least 16 years old with a 2.0 GPA, excellent attendance and a counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply in 11th grade through your school; contact the citywide Cooperative Education coordinator (773-553-2108) for the process.
notes: Placement and training partners listed on the page include Genesys Works and Urban Alliance. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age is 16. Cutting school or work can cost credit.

name: CPS Early College: dual credit and dual enrollment at City Colleges of Chicago
org: Chicago Public Schools and City Colleges of Chicago
pay_detail: Free college credit. The page says you earn college credit for free.
duration: Per semester; dual enrollment is one course per semester at a City Colleges campus
deadline_text: Register once per academic year. Deadlines not stated; talk to your counselor early.
who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled at a Chicago Public Schools high school, including home-schooled students per City Colleges. A 2.5 GPA and strong attendance are typical requirements. If your GPA is lower, the page says recommendation letters are accepted. Under 16 needs a principal recommendation and approval from the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, get approval from the dual enrollment coordinator at your City Colleges campus, complete the City Colleges application and pick classes. Do not pay for or enroll in a class before talking to the Early College team.
notes: Undocumented students are eligible (CPS page). Some courses need ACT, SAT or City Colleges placement scores; many courses have no prerequisites. Jumpstart Pathways and Runway 606 are related CPS options. Seven campuses; each has a dual enrollment coordinator.

name: Chicago Police and Firefighter Training Academy (CPFTA)
org: Chicago Public Schools with Chicago Police, Fire and City Colleges
grades: Apply in 10th grade; program runs 11th and 12th grade
pay_detail: Free: uniforms, materials, snacks and transportation help provided; scholarships possible. A paid summer internship between junior and senior year is possible (pay not stated).
duration: Two years; Tuesday and Wednesday 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., September to May
deadline_text: The application for the class of 2028 is closed. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February; recruitment events run in February and March. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in Chicago and attend a Chicago high school (public, private or homeschooled). A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 recommendation letters, a physical and a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, a signed consent form, a copy of a school or state ID, 2 recommendation letters, a physical exam record and a background check.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.

name: College Now
pay_detail: Free. The CUNY page describes College Now as a FREE program.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
deadline_text: Each campus sets its own deadline. CUNY says spring applications are typically available October to early February, summer March to June, and fall late March to mid-September.
who_can_apply: Students at NYC public high schools. Grade 11 and 12 with an 80+ GPA can take courses on the partner campus, and a 70+ GPA opens some courses. Grade 10 with a 70+ GPA can take non-credit college and career awareness courses only. College Now is geared toward NYC Public Schools 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply to a specific CUNY campus's College Now program. Talk to your school's College Now liaison if your school has a partner campus, or contact a campus program directly. Many programs are first come, first served.
notes: Graduating seniors cannot join summer sessions. Students in Early College high schools can only join in summer. Costs beyond tuition (like textbooks) are not described on the CUNY page, so ask the campus.

name: Cupertino Teen Commission
duration: Two-year staggered terms
deadline_text: The city page says recruitment is currently closed. No reopening date is stated.
who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are incoming 8th to 11th graders. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday, in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term; the 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.

name: Lifeguard Training, Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor
pay_detail: Course fees apply. Amounts are not on the page; check the Rec Guide or online registration.
duration: varies by course
deadline_text: Courses are offered throughout the year. Check WebTrac for sessions.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the course. Junior Lifeguarding: pass a swim skills check on day one (25 yards of front crawl and breaststroke, tread water 1 minute, and more). Junior Swim Instructor: no age or swim test listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Training can lead to City of Davis aquatics work. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later, with volunteer chances after the training. The page does not promise a job. Lifeguard certification needs full attendance and passing tests. Job minimum ages are set in each posting at cityofdavis.org/jobs.

name: Davis Junior Basketball Coach, Official and Score Keeper
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: $17.39 an hour
duration: 6-week season starting the week of January 18, 2027
deadline_text: The posting is open continuously. Mandatory training is the week of January 4, 2027 and a coaching clinic on January 9, 2027.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.

name: Davis Senior High CTE Pathways
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Enroll through your counselor during normal course selection.
who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab (see the Internship and Career Development Course).
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.

name: Teen Leadership Council
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period was extended to Oct 2, 2026 and is now closed. The next call is not posted.
who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.

name: De Anza College Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply for admission before the quarter you want; see the De Anza academic calendar.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.

name: DECA (high school division)
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join anytime through your advisor.
who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.

name: Teen Advisory Board (DeKalb County Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours for attending meetings.
duration: Monthly meetings for the school year; at least one meeting must be in person
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-2027 school year are closed. The page does not say when the next application opens.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who live in DeKalb County.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps; check the library's Teens Get Involved page and volunteer page for the next cycle.
notes: Meeting dates were listed as coming soon. Members can miss a meeting by telling advisors through Slack or the pre-meeting survey. A search result also described a separate Teen Library Board Trustee seat, but that was not on the page read.

name: DeKalb Summer Youth Employment Program (DSYEP)
org: DeKalb County Government and WorkSource DeKalb
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2025
duration: About 4 weeks (June 2 to July 3 in 2025)
deadline_text: In 2025 registration ran Apr 10 to Apr 20 (11:59 p.m.). No 2026 or 2027 cycle was found on the county site.
who_can_apply: 2025 rules: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 21 who pass a drug screening and background check. Interns were picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: In 2025, online registration at dekalbcountyga.gov/dsyep. That address now leads to a registration form marked no longer active. For help the 2025 county release listed the Workforce Development Manager at (470) 572-8229.
notes: Confirm that a new cycle exists before planning around it. All dates, pay and rules here are from the 2025 county release. WorkSource DeKalb also lists youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers as a service group and sends people to ATLworks.org to check eligibility. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Discovery Cube Orange County Teen Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.
duration: At least one four-hour shift every 30 days. 60 hours of service before the Cube verifies your hours.
deadline_text: Teen application is closed right now. The page says to check back on December 1, 2026 for winter/spring 2027 details.
who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need verified service hours. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.

name: Internship and Career Development Course
fields: any; health; education; engineering; law-government; arts-media
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. 2026-27 sites are listed now.
who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.

name: Dublin L.E.A.D. Summer Program
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.

name: Dublin Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
grades: Enrolled in middle school or high school
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 seats are filled (term June 2026 to May 2027). The city page we read does not post a recruitment date for the 2027-28 term.
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page we read. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.

name: EBAYC Volunteers and Student Internships
deadline_text: Not posted
who_can_apply: Not stated.
how_to_apply: The home page links to a volunteer page on ebayc.org. Contact EBAYC directly.
notes: The home page says it welcomes volunteers, volunteer groups and student internships but gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it did not load (404) on Oct 7, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

name: EBMUD High School Summer Internship (HSSI)
city: Oakland, CA and EBMUD service area
pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)
duration: 6 weeks, mid-June through August, about 16 hours a week
deadline_text: 2026 East Bay program: no direct applications, referrals from partner groups only. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.

name: East Bay Regional Park District Youth and Student Jobs
city: Oakland, CA and parks across Alameda and Contra Costa counties
pay_detail: Pay is not posted on the youth pages. See each job posting.
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No jobs were posted on governmentjobs.com on Oct 7, 2026. Watch ebparks.org/jobs/youth and governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks.
who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.

name: Elgin Community College Dual Credit
pay_detail: Accelerate College: no tuition for district-approved courses. Independent enrollment and Dual Enrollment: students are usually billed tuition. Career tech courses the district does not approve require tuition.
duration: Per semester
deadline_text: No deadline on the ECC page. Talk with your high school counselor about dates.
who_can_apply: Students at participating schools: U-46 (Bartlett, Elgin, Larkin, South Elgin, Streamwood), District 300 (Dundee-Crown, Hampshire, Jacobs), District 301 (Burlington Central), District 303 (St. Charles East, St. Charles North, Compass Academy), Cambridge Lakes Charter and St. Edward Central Catholic. The tracks are for juniors, seniors, or juniors and seniors, depending on the track. Talk with your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk with your parents and your high school counselor first, then use the online Dual Credit application (Apply Now). Independent enrollment also needs approval from the ECC Dual Credit office. Contact: DualCredit@elgin.edu or 847-214-7887.
notes: Accelerate College students may need to qualify for college-level courses and testing may be required. Each district publishes a Dual Credit Guide listing what its schools support. The ECC page also lists Upward Bound, Educational Talent Search and College and Career Readiness workshops.

name: Upward Bound at Elgin Community College
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.
duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Dundee-Crown, Larkin or Streamwood High School who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and are either potential first-generation college students or from a low-income household (U.S. Department of Education rules). If unsure, apply and staff will tell you if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Student and parent or guardian complete the online Upward Bound application. Counselors and teachers can fill out the Student Recommendation Form. Contact: upwardbound@elgin.edu, 847-214-7253, Building K, Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin.
notes: Only for students at the three listed high schools. The page does not mention a summer part or a start date, so ask staff. A web search snippet suggested Elgin High School is also served, but the ECC page itself lists only the three above.

name: Youth Environmental Academy and Internships
pay_detail: Paid; rate not posted
duration: 8 weeks (summer) or 12 weeks (spring)
deadline_text: No dates on the Ecology Center page. Berkeley YouthWorks listed a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026 and said Summer 2027 information comes in Feb 2027, but that page does not mention this academy.
who_can_apply: Berkeley residents ages 15 to 24, recruited through Berkeley YouthWorks.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Berkeley YouthWorks interest form (the Ecology Center sends you there). Contact alex@ecologycenter.org or 510-697-4808.
notes: Berkeley residents only. YouthWorks asks for an interest form and a 15 to 20 minute interview. Pay rate and exact academy dates are not posted.

name: Eden Area ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
fields: education; food-hospitality; health; law-government; tech-cs; trades; business-finance
duration: Classes are held Monday to Friday; course length varies by class
deadline_text: Enroll through your home school counselor; the page gives no class start dates.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending high school in the Castro Valley, Hayward, San Leandro or San Lorenzo Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Ask your home high school counselor to contact the Eden Area ROP career counselor at (510) 293-2973. Main office (510) 293-2900.
notes: Center is at 26316 Hesperian Blvd, Hayward. Cost, pay and ages are not stated on the page. Some pathways are offered only at certain high schools. Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.

name: El Camino Health Junior Auxiliary
city: Mountain View and Los Gatos, CA
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 1 year
deadline_text: No application deadline posted. The page says to check back in mid-January 2027 for signup for the next Junior Application Seminar.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. Competitive, with limited spots. No summer-only option.
how_to_apply: Attend the annual application seminar, then apply. Info on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Hospital does not offer summer-only or programs shorter than one year. Locations are Mountain View and Los Gatos. Spots are limited (earlier check).

name: Elk Grove Youth Commission
duration: Meets 2nd Tuesday, Sept to May, 6:00 pm, Elk Grove Council Chambers
deadline_text: No open recruitment as of Oct 7, 2026. Seats are filled when openings come up, and the City posts a notice with a Youth Commission application.
who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages read, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens.

name: Summer VolunTEEN Program (Emory Healthcare)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No program fee stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks (June 1 to July 24 in 2026), one shift per week, Monday to Thursday, at least 4 hours
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened Feb 17 and closed Feb 27, 2026 (or earlier if full). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 as of June 1 of the program year (June 1, 2026 on the current page).
how_to_apply: Create a MyImpact account and complete the application, with student and parent signatures on four forms. Get a recommendation from a teacher or school counselor by the deadline and rank up to three hospital locations. Interview, health screening and orientation follow.
notes: The window was only 10 days in 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting in early 2027. Space is limited and waitlists happen. Health screening includes a TB test and proof of chickenpox and measles immunity. No shadowing, internships or clinical hours.

name: Emory Pre-College Program
pay_detail: 2026 prices: 2-week noncredit course $5,510 residential or $3,925 commuter; 3-week institute $8,264 residential; 4 weeks $11,020. $70 application fee. 2027 prices not posted.
duration: 2 to 6 weeks (2027 noncredit sessions June 13 to 26, June 27 to July 10, July 11 to 24)
deadline_text: Applications for 2027 open in December 2026. Deadlines: noncredit sessions May 3, 2027; Pre-Med Institute Feb 1, 2027; credit Summer College April 20 and June 7, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students; the page says it serves current sophomores and juniors. Application needs transcript and recommendations.
how_to_apply: Choose a program and course, review costs, then start the online application (transcript, recommendations, $70 fee). After acceptance, complete the pre-arrival checklist and pay the $350 enrollment deposit.
notes: Expensive. The nearest deadline is the Pre-Med Institute on Feb 1, 2027 (deadline_iso shows the main May 3 date). Financial aid deadline was May 1 in 2026. Information sessions are in November and December 2026.

name: Evergreen Valley College Dual Enrollment and CCAP
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page.
who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED, with approval from your school counselor or principal. Adult school students in GED programs can also join.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.

name: Exploring (Learning for Life career posts)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Fees are not stated on the site; ask the post.
duration: Meets regularly
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line.

name: High School Internships (Facciotti Lab)
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.
deadline_text: No application process or dates posted.
who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.

name: Fermilab PRISM (Program for Research, Innovation, and STEM Mentorship)
grades: Rising high school senior (senior in 2027-28) or 2027 high school graduate
pay_detail: $500 per week stipend. Housing is not provided; transportation assistance is available.
duration: 4 weeks, July 12 to Aug 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications open Jan 12, 2027 and close Mar 1, 2027 (recommendation letter also due Mar 1). Offers Apr 12, 2027; accept by Apr 21, 2027.
who_can_apply: Illinois high school students who will be seniors in 2027-28 or who graduate in 2027. Must be a U.S. citizen and have proof of medical insurance. No STEM prerequisites. Age and GPA are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal, a supplemental questionnaire, a PDF list of your STEM courses uploaded in the Resume section, and one letter from a STEM teacher or STEM club advisor. You cannot upload missing items after you submit.
notes: The apply link only works during the application window. Recommenders get an email upload link that is sent only on weekdays during business hours, so line up your letter writer early. A walkthrough video is on the program page.

name: Fermilab VALOR JROTC Summer Internship
grades: Illinois JROTC high school junior, senior or recent graduate
pay_detail: $18 per hour. No onsite housing or transportation reimbursement.
duration: 6 weeks, June 28 to Aug 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications opened Oct 5, 2026 and close Feb 5, 2027. Offers Mar 15, 2027; accept by Mar 22, 2027.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in an Illinois high school JROTC program, and an Illinois high school junior, senior or recent graduate when you apply. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal with an unofficial transcript, a resume and three short essay answers (under 200 words each). Then give contact info for one recommendation writer; the letter is due by the close date. Questions: Internships@fnal.gov.
notes: Only for cadets in an Illinois JROTC program. You cannot upload missing items after you submit, so gather everything first. Reference emails go out only on weekdays during business hours.

name: Fernbank Youth Interpreters (FYI) Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time $50 fee after acceptance, which can be waived for those who qualify.
duration: One year, June 1 to May 31, at least 45 hours
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications are closed. The museum expects to post information on the 2027-28 program in February 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 by September 1 and no older than 17 by June 1. Volunteers who turn 18 during the year may finish it.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application, an essay written by the teen, and two reference forms. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Contact: FYI@FernbankMuseum.org or 404-929-6360.
notes: Described as very competitive; teens who are not accepted are encouraged to reapply the next year.

name: Trailblazers -N- Training
org: City of Folsom Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Fee not stated in the news post.
duration: 8 weekly sessions (2026: June 8 to July 31, Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:00)
deadline_text: 2026 post went up May 22, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.

name: Foothill College High School Dual Enrollment
city: Los Altos Hills and Sunnyvale, CA
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.
duration: One quarter at a time
deadline_text: No single deadline stated. Submit the form before you register each quarter.
who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).

name: Forage Virtual Job Simulations
pay_detail: Free
duration: Self-paced, usually a few hours
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open access and free. The page does not state an age minimum, so check the terms and the Minors privacy notice.
how_to_apply: Create a free account and pick a simulation at theforage.com.
notes: Good for a resume line, but it is not a job or an internship. The page has no age minimum and links a privacy notice for minors, so read the terms and ask a parent before signing up.

name: Fremont Unified Career and Technical Education
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No dates stated. Choose courses at your school.
who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining career and technical education programs.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general: 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways, and it does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.

name: Fremont Youth Advisory Commission
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or residency rules. Ask the Recreation Division.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call the Recreation Division at 510-494-4300.
notes: Meets 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the first Monday of each month except July and August, at City Hall, 3300 Capitol Ave. The page lists 12 members.

name: Teen Volunteers (Fulton County Library System)
org: Fulton County Library System (Atlanta-Fulton Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts after orientation
deadline_text: Applications are always accepted, but most projects are full and most locations have a waitlist.
who_can_apply: Youth under 18 may apply with a parent or guardian signature. The page does not state a minimum age, so ask Volunteer Services.
how_to_apply: Under 18: download and print the PDF application, sign it, get a parent or guardian signature, and return it to Volunteer Services by email, mail, fax or drop-off. Then attend orientation. Email vol.services@fultoncountyga.gov or call 404-613-0125.
notes: The page says the library is currently on hold for community service hour requirements, so students who need school hours must contact Volunteer Services early. Teen Advisory Boards exist at some branches; ask the Youth Services Librarian. Library Systems for DeKalb and Cobb counties are separate.

name: Work-Based Learning, Fulton County Schools
pay_detail: School credit. The district page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: Per school term
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator for the application window.
who_can_apply: Fulton County Schools students who are at least 16, in 11th or 12th grade, and following a defined career pathway. Individual schools may add rules. Students in Atlanta Public Schools use their own district.
how_to_apply: Print and finish the WBL Interest Form and give it to your school's WBL coordinator. Students who meet the requirements are issued an application. Grades, attendance, discipline and related coursework are reviewed. You must follow up on job leads yourself.
notes: District contact listed on the page: Leslie McHann, 470-254-0466. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Teen Volunteers at Gail Borden Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
