duration: Short sessions, about 1 hour each; you pick the ones you want
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A teen volunteer orientation is listed for Sunday, Oct 18, 1:00 to 1:30 PM at the Main Library Conference Room (the page does not print the year; Oct 18 is a Sunday in 2026).
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. Bring an ID (school ID, driver's license or library card).
how_to_apply: 1) Fill out the online teen volunteer application. 2) Register for a one-time Teen Volunteer Orientation. 3) Sign up for open sessions on the teen volunteer calendar. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead.
notes: Grade 6 is under 13, so younger readers should ask about their grade. The library's Elgin Teens page also describes Studio 270, a high school teen space at 270 N. Grove Ave. (homework help, college readiness, job hunting help; phone 847-695-7577), but parts of that page look out of date, so call first. The volunteer page lists a contact email that is hidden in the page text; use the library's Contact Us page.

name: Work-Based Learning (Internships), Gwinnett County Public Schools
pay_detail: School credit. The GCPS page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: One semester at a time as a school elective
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Forms go to your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator; ask when the next semester deadline is.
who_can_apply: Gwinnett County Public Schools juniors and seniors who are 16 by September 1 and have coursework that matches their career choice. The school reviews grades, attendance and discipline.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. Forms: electronic agreement, WBL application, recommendation form and job site information form. Forms are uploaded in the WBL class when the semester starts. Apprenticeships need a post-high-school plan.
notes: No home-office or private-residence placements. The program cannot guarantee a job. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Genesys Works Bay Area Internship Program
regions: east-bay; national; oakland; san-francisco; san-jose; silicon-valley
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
deadline_text: No dates posted. Applicants get an interview, then summer skills training.
who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages read. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.

name: Volunteens at Geneva Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Fall 2026 session: Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026
deadline_text: Fall 2026 session runs Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026. No registration deadline is listed. Dates for the next session are not posted.
who_can_apply: Geneva Public Library patrons in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register as a Volunteen using the sign-up form on the page. Contact: geneva.library@gpld.org or (630) 232-0780, 227 S. Seventh St., Geneva.
notes: Service hours are flexible and are not listed as a set number. The page does not describe the registration steps beyond the sign-up form.

name: Teen Volunteer Program (Georgia Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid. $45 administrative fee (check or money order) once accepted. Perks: volunteer pass, free parking on shifts, 5 one-time daily tickets after finishing.
duration: 4 months per session: Spring (Jan to Apr) 60 hours, Summer (May to Aug) 80 hours, Fall (Sep to Dec) 60 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 session starts onboarding with information sessions in October 2026; dates not posted yet. The 2026 summer/fall cycle on the page: info sessions in July, application deadline Aug 1, interviews Aug 16, orientation Sept 12.
who_can_apply: High school or home school students ages 15 to 17 at the time of application. Teens need their own transportation and a parent or guardian must join the info session.
how_to_apply: Register for one mandatory virtual information session (email volunteer@georgiaaquarium.org or use the page's Contact Us interest form). A parent or guardian must attend with the teen. If chosen, attend a group interview. Bring birth certificate and photo ID.
notes: Not every applicant gets an interview. No behind-the-scenes roles for teens and no court-ordered or school service hours. The page lists the group interview as both three hours and four hours, and its weekday names for the 2026 dates do not match the calendar, so confirm exact dates with the Aquarium. Last-year dates are shown for reference only.

name: STEP: Science, Technology and Engineering Program (Georgia Tech Aerospace Engineering)
org: Georgia Tech Daniel Guggenheim School of Aerospace Engineering
pay_detail: Free to students (funded by industry donors). No stipend stated. Students provide their own daily transportation.
duration: 2-week day program (not residential); Atlanta session July 6 to 17 in 2026
deadline_text: 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are at least 16 years old by the program start. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the STEP page before the deadline. Questions: outreach@ae.gatech.edu.
notes: Read on the Georgia Space Grant Consortium page that hosts the STEP information; the Georgia Tech Aerospace page itself returned a 403 block. Other sessions listed for 2026 were in Augusta and Albany.

name: Georgia Work-Based Learning (including Youth Apprenticeship)
org: Georgia Department of Education, Career, Technical and Agricultural Education
pay_detail: Co-op and Youth Apprenticeship are paid work-site experiences. Internships may be paid or unpaid.
duration: Varies by option. An Employability Skill Development placement can last up to one school year.
deadline_text: Set by each school or district. No state dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students, through their own school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. The state page lists no age or grade rules. Districts set their own (Gwinnett, Fulton County and Cobb above say juniors and seniors age 16 or older).
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator or counselor. Internships can happen only after coursework related to the placement. Co-op students must be enrolled in a course directly related to the job.
notes: Youth Apprenticeship in Georgia is run through the Department of Education and local schools. The Georgia Department of Labor youth page covers work permits and child labor rules only. Georgia Work Ready was not researched. Georgia requires a work permit for students under 16 (see the Georgia Department of Labor work permit page).

name: Teen Gallery Guides @ Getty
org: J. Paul Getty Museum (Getty Center and Getty Villa)
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
deadline_text: The page says the application window typically opens in early February each year. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend, so ask whether a California work permit is needed.

name: Girls Inc. of Alameda County High School Programs
city: Oakland, CA (and Cal State East Bay, Hayward)
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact Girls Inc.
who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: Code the Game is a six week program (the page mentions a fall offering). Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.

name: Girls Who Code Clubs and Pathways
grades: Clubs: grades 3 to 12 (split 3 to 5 and 6 to 12). Pathways: high school.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
deadline_text: Ongoing.
who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.

name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay / Silicon Valley: Volunteer
org: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page
deadline_text: Ongoing. No sign-up deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sacramento: Individual Volunteers (Construction and ReStore)
org: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)
deadline_text: Rolling. Sign up for shifts after orientation.
who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.

name: Hack Club
pay_detail: Free
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: Join anytime.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
pay_detail: Free
duration: All of October 2026
deadline_text: Runs through October 2026; sign in with MyMLH.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.

name: HandsOn Bay Area Youth Volunteering (HandsOn Tomorrow paused)
grades: High school (for HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Council)
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
deadline_text: Monthly projects: sign up on the Community Calendar. HandsOn Tomorrow will not run in summer 2026 and no later dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), is paused and is not running in summer 2026. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.

name: ZooTeen Program at Happy Hollow Park and Zoo
org: Happy Hollow Park and Zoo (City of San Jose)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed seasonally. The last orientation listed on the page was Oct 18, 2025 (old); no 2026-27 date is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps but is not required.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.

name: H.A.R.D. Volunteer Program (Hayward Area Recreation and Park District)
org: Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.)
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.
deadline_text: Opportunities are posted throughout the year. No closing date is stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).

name: Hayward Public Library Teen Volunteer Opportunities
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted during the school year. No closing date is stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.

name: Hayward Youth Commission
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall on the second Monday of each month, September to June, except holidays. The 2021 notice said two-year terms.
deadline_text: 2025 cycle: applications due Friday, May 9, 2025. Interviews were on Friday, May 30, 2025. No 2026 cycle was found.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.

name: Hidden Genius Project Immersion Program
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed
duration: 15 months
deadline_text: The application page says applications are currently closed and to follow HGP social media or the newsletter for the 2027 application. The last posted deadline was Feb 21, 2025.
who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The immersion page still shows the old 2025 deadline. No 2027 date is posted, so wait for the new announcement. Oakland and Richmond are the East Bay sites.

name: Teen Leadership Council (High Museum of Art)
pay_detail: Described as a paid position; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: One-year commitment, including a 6-week summer intensive (June 3 to July 17 in 2026), Wednesday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., plus regular meetings
deadline_text: 2026-27 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed at midnight March 1 (2026); applicants were told by May 1, 2026. The page does not post the 2027-28 cycle.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors enrolled full time in high school for the program year. The group has 15 members.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application during the Feb 1 to Mar 1 window. Questions: HMATeenPrograms@high.org.
notes: No absences are allowed during the summer intensive. The High's Teens and College page also lists an Early College Program in Art History and Curatorial Studies with the Atlanta University Center for rising juniors and seniors, but it gave no dates or application details.

name: Hiller Aviation Museum Flight Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
deadline_text: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.

name: Hire LA's Youth
org: City of Los Angeles Economic and Workforce Development Department (EWDD)
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
deadline_text: The site banner says it is accepting applications but gives no dates, and its document library page still shows a 2022 summer banner. Call EWDD at 213-744-7300 to confirm the current cycle.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF we read (2024 version) lists the other eligibility rules, so check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before counting on a summer 2027 spot. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24 (school help, job readiness, some paid internships); ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit.

name: Hoag Jr. Auxiliary / Candystripers (High School Volunteer)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The program is full. The page says to check back January 2027 for when interest forms will be taken again.
who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. Specific weekly hours are not stated on the page.

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
grades: Secondary and college students (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your health science teacher.
who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.

name: Humane Society Silicon Valley Student Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.

name: Huntington Beach Public Library Teen Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
deadline_text: Most roles take online applications with no deadline. The Teen Tech role lists applications Aug 29 to Sep 12 and interviews Sep 15 to 18, but the page gives no year, so check the date.
who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens (Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center, OC Coastkeeper cleanups) with their own age rules, so read it for those. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.

name: Illinois Boys State (American Legion)
grades: High school juniors (finished at least one semester of 11th grade)
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
duration: One week, June 12 to 18, 2027 (90th annual session)
deadline_text: The registration page says registration for the 2027 session closes at 4:00 PM on June 12, 2027, when the session starts. Ask your local Legion post about its earlier sponsor deadline.
who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.

name: ALA Illini Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Illinois
city: Illinois (location not stated on the site)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages we read. Ask the Illinois Girls State office and your local American Legion Auxiliary unit.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: Next session is June 20 to 26, 2027. The application deadline is not stated on the pages read; contact the Department office.
who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.

name: Irvine Public Library Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Summer Reading volunteers work a weekly two-hour shift. Other roles vary.
deadline_text: The undated page says: Summer Reading applications ran May 9 to May 30, school-year roles reopen Saturday, August 1, and TAG is full with a wait list for applications after August 26. No year is shown, so confirm current openings.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and over (program assistance and toy cleaning are ages 14 to 17). Teen Summer Reading volunteers are students in grades 8 to 11. Each library has up to 20 TAG memberships.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application on the library's volunteer system. A required orientation comes before the summer program.
notes: The page lists no library contact; it points to the volunteer coordinator, and the City of Irvine main number is 949-724-6000. The page writes the application link as volgistics.com/appform/337674493 (search for it on the volunteer system).

name: JA Launchpad (Junior Achievement, Fremont)
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)
deadline_text: The page says the center is Coming Early 2027. No opening date or sign-up is posted.
who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.

name: Job Corps Sacramento Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).
deadline_text: Ongoing enrollment. No dates posted on the Sacramento page.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.

name: John Muir Health High School Student Volunteer Program (Walnut Creek Medical Center)
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
deadline_text: No application window is stated on the official page. Contact a partner high school (for example Acalanes, Campolindo, Las Lomas, Miramonte, Monte Vista, San Ramon Valley or Ygnacio Valley) to ask about the next intake.
who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.

name: Junior Achievement of Northern California (high school programs)
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No central deadline; ask JA.
who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages read, so ask JA.

name: KP LAUNCH High School Program
city: Northern California Kaiser Permanente service areas
regions: silicon-valley; san-jose; peninsula; fremont; east-bay; oakland; san-francisco; sacramento

duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
deadline_text: Opens Nov 16, 2026 at 9am Pacific; closes Jan 8, 2027 at 5pm Pacific.
who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive (a Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, not confirmed here). Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.

name: Kane County Workforce Development Youth Services (WIOA Youth)
city: Kane, DeKalb and Kendall Counties (Elgin area), IL

duration: Varies by provider

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc.; Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.

Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.

name: Key Club (high school service club)
pay_detail: No pay. Members pay nominal dues (amount not listed on the pages read).
deadline_text: Join your school's club or start one. No cycle stated.
who_can_apply: Any high school student who wants to serve and lead. Clubs are set up in high schools or equivalent schools. Members are expected to do at least 50 hours of service a year.
how_to_apply: Use the Find a Key Club tool on keyclub.org, or follow the Start a Key Club steps if your school has none.
notes: Dues and local rules vary by club; dues amount not stated on the pages read. Key Club International phone: 800-549-2647.

name: Khan Academy college and careers courses
pay_detail: Free (the site says it is a nonprofit offering free education)
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open to anyone. The site says its mission is a free education for anyone, anywhere. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Go to the page, pick a course, and sign up for a free account if you want to save progress.
notes: The page loads slowly because it builds in your browser. Course list seen: Financial Literacy, Personal Finance, Entrepreneurship, Careers, College admissions, Career Exploration.

name: Kode With Klossy
city: Virtual and in-person (Oakland, San Francisco and more)
pay_detail: Free

deadline_text: Sign-ups are open for Code-a-Bration (Nov 7 to 8, 2026 in Oakland and virtual; Oct 17 to 18 in Chicago and virtual). Summer 2027 Camp applications open in February 2027; closing dates not posted.

how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form linked on the Kode With Klossy programs page.
notes: Free for all programs. Workforce development programs are for ages 18 to 26, not high schoolers. Camp dates and sites for summer 2027 are not posted yet.

name: LA County Library Teen Volunteer and Teen Advisory Board
org: County of Los Angeles Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid; students can earn school service credit.
duration: Varies by library
deadline_text: No deadline. Ask your local LA County Library about current openings.
who_can_apply: Anyone 14 and older can volunteer. Teen Advisory Boards are open to teens at libraries that have one.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LA County Library branch to ask about volunteer openings and whether it has a Teen Advisory Board.
notes: This covers LA County Library branches (unincorporated areas and many cities), not the City of Los Angeles library system (see the LAPL card). Tasks vary by branch and season.

name: LA County Youth@Work
org: LA County Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO)
pay_detail: Paid work experience for about 140 hours plus a class. The page does not state an hourly wage.
duration: About 160 hours in all: up to 140 hours of paid work plus 20 hours of job-readiness class
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Fill out the youth interest form and an AJCC contacts you within 48 hours. In 2025 the summer jobs started July 1.
who_can_apply: LA County residents who are 14 to 24 when they enroll and have the legal right to work in the U.S. The county gives priority to youth with high needs, such as current or former foster youth, youth touched by the justice system, youth who are or were homeless, and LGBTQ+ youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Interest Form on the Youth@Work page. AJCC staff reach out within 48 hours to check eligibility and match you with an employer.
notes: The county released a Youth@Work Program Review and Redesign Report on August 25, 2026, so rules and pay for 2027 may change. Under 18 you need a California work permit before the first day. The pay figure is the 2025 summer rate from the county's own news release, not a 2027 promise. Long Beach youth can also use the City of Long Beach center (see the LBWIN card).

name: LACMA Teens
org: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
pay_detail: Selected teens receive a stipend. The amount is not stated.
duration: 10 sessions on select Sundays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Oct 2026 to Feb 2027
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort: applications ran July 1 to Aug 21, 2026 (5 p.m.) and are closed. The page says LACMA will not accept applications again until next year.
who_can_apply: Los Angeles County residents, 16 to 18, who will be juniors or seniors in the 2027 school year and are interested in art, museums or community events.
how_to_apply: Online application during the open window (last year July 1 to Aug 21). Questions go to teens@lacma.org.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted; watch for a July opening. LACMA also offers NexGenLA, a free membership for LA County youth 17 and under (free museum entry plus one guest). Whether the stipend counts as wages for work-permit purposes is not stated, so ask the program.

name: Lao Family Community Development: Youth on the Move
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage (MSYEP rule); exact rate not posted
duration: Up to about 100 hours
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Summer 2026 round is over; call for the next cycle.
who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per the City of Oakland summer youth jobs partner table. Oakland residency is required for that program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 533-8850 or 1 (833) 532-3674, or use the Contact Us form at lfcd.org.
notes: LFCD's own employment page does not describe this youth program. Ages, hours and pay come from the City of Oakland MSYEP page. Under-18 workers need a work permit.

name: LAPL Teen Volunteer, Teen Council and Teens Leading Change
pay_detail: Unpaid; you earn community service hours.
duration: Varies by branch; Teen Council members complete at least 20 community service hours
deadline_text: No deadline. Teens Leading Change projects form in September, but you can join anytime.
who_can_apply: Teen Volunteer and Teens Leading Change are for ages 14 to 19. Teen Council is for ages 11 to 19. Volunteers fill out a Teen Volunteer Intake Form and a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
how_to_apply: Contact the Young Adult Librarian or Senior Librarian at your nearest library, then complete the intake form and parent waiver. Questions: Volunteer Engagement, 213-228-7490.
notes: LAPL hosts over 2,600 teen volunteers a year across 73 branches, and openings differ by branch. Some branches also have volunteer slots listed at volunteer.lapl.org.

name: Summer Youth Volunteer Program
org: Livermore Area Recreation and Park District (LARPD)
pay_detail: Volunteer position. Earn community service hours; no wage is listed.
duration: Summer weekly shifts. The 2026 FAQ says sign-ups start with a maximum of 2 weeks, with more weeks added later.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: sign up for orientation by Friday, March 13, 2026. Orientations were March 19, 2026 (5 to 6:30 pm) and March 25, 2026 (4 to 5:30 pm) at the Robert Livermore Community Center. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Youth Volunteer Waiver. Students must attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation. Some roles have extra rules: Summer Nature Camp requires the Counselor in Training (CIT) program, and Open Space Jr. Docents require age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Create a LARPD volunteer account by submitting the General Volunteer Application (use a personal email, not a school email). Attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation at the Robert Livermore Community Center. Then sign up for shifts through MyImpactPage. Questions: volunteer@larpd.org.
notes: The 2026 cycle is closed. Watch larpd.org/volunteer and the orientation pages for the 2027 dates; the district's pages were not all updated to the same year. The FAQ says the opportunity list may change each year. The orientation and FAQ pages list volunteer@larpd.org as the contact. Not a paid job, so no California work permit is needed.

name: Las Positas College CCAP Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: Free; tuition and fees waived and required materials provided (parking may cost extra for classes at LPC)
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
who_can_apply: High school students in partner districts: Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley, plus San Ramon Valley USD (welding) and TUSD (fire safety training). Residency and citizenship rules apply; ask Admissions & Records.
how_to_apply: Sign the CCAP Dual Enrollment form (once for all of high school) with your school counselor. Questions: lpc-dualenrollment@laspositascollege.edu.
notes: Offered during and after the school day. Ages are not stated on the page.

name: Berkeley Lab Director's Apprenticeship Program (BLDAP)

who_can_apply: Grades 10 and 11. Public school students in Alameda, San Francisco and Contra Costa counties are prioritized; nearby counties are encouraged to apply. In person at Berkeley Lab at least 4 days a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Berkeley Lab K-12 program page when it opens (the 2026 application ran through apply.mykaleidoscope.com).
notes: Whether students are paid is not stated. Finishing students can join later workshops and possible lab internships in following summers.

name: Experiences in Research

duration: 6 weeks (June 15 to July 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 window was Feb 2 to Mar 22, 2026. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: Grades 10 to 12 in Northern California, at least 16 by the program start. Students within 30 miles of the lab are prioritized. You can do the program only once.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window and pick your top three projects. Do not contact mentors directly. Oakland Unified students also fill out a supplemental application.
notes: The page still says 'at least 16 by June 16, 2025', so check the age date when it reopens. Some 2026 projects were hybrid or virtual. Under-18 interns need a work permit.

name: SeA Bilingual STEM Camp

deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; no 2027 dates posted.

how_to_apply: Watch the Berkeley Lab K-12 high school programs page.
notes: Grades and ages are not listed on the page. The 2026 camp is over and no 2027 camp is posted, so it is not confirmed to repeat. Page says it can lead to summer internship chances.

name: LBWIN Youth Career Services Center
org: City of Long Beach Economic Development and Opportunity, Workforce Development Bureau
pay_detail: Paid internships and Youth@Work (about 160 hours of paid work experience). Pay rates are not stated. Workshops and career help are free.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. The competitive school-to-career programs (Long Beach Public Service Corps, Port of Long Beach internship, Fire Corps internship and others) open for set application periods.
who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 30. Youth@Work is for ages 14 to 24 and WIOA Youth services are listed for ages 16 to 24. WIOA funding focuses on out-of-school youth with barriers such as low income, foster care, homelessness, juvenile justice involvement, parenting, or a disability. A Long Beach residency rule is not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Complete the Youth Interest Form on the city's Youth Services page. Partner agencies can also refer youth through the Unite Us platform.
notes: Because most WIOA funding targets youth facing barriers, a teen still in school may be steered to Youth@Work or a school-to-career program instead. Under 18 you need a California work permit for any paid placement. The city's Youth Opportunities page also lists teen volunteering at Long Beach libraries and at Parks, Recreation and Marine (ages 13 and up).

name: League of Volunteers Teen Volunteers (Summer Recreation)

notes: The teen call on the homepage is for summer 2026. Confirm with the League whether it recruits again for 2027. Serves the Tri-Cities (Fremont, Newark and Union City).

The municipal code gives 15 youth seats and 3 adult seats; the code does not say how seats are filled.

The lahstalon.org article is a 2024 news piece, used only for the interview and volunteer details. The museum's adult docent roles are separate and not for teens.

name: Los Rios Dual Enrollment and CCAP (American River, Cosumnes River, Folsom Lake, Sacramento City)
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Other fees may apply, such as the student representation fee. Books may cost extra.
duration: Per semester
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply and register by each college's term dates.

how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, pick the Los Rios college that offers the class, apply at that college as a dual enrollment student (parent signature and principal recommendation needed), then register.
notes: Credits go on a permanent college transcript. Whether you also get high school credit depends on your school, so ask your counselor. Your school does not need a CCAP agreement for you to take a college class. Application deadlines are by college term.

name: Major League Hacking (MLH) hackathons
pay_detail: Event costs are not listed on the pages read; check each event. The Fellowship pays a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Weekend events; Fellowship is 12 weeks

how_to_apply: Browse the events list on mlh.com and read each event's age rule before registering.
notes: The pages read did not state a minimum age. Many MLH events are aimed at college students, so check before you plan travel.

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG), Menlo Park Library
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.
deadline_text: Rolling membership. The page is accepting applications for new members and states no deadline.

how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.

name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC), City of Menlo Park
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services Department
grades: Entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.

deadline_text: Closed for 2026-27. The 2026-27 window ran May through July 2026 (page lists a July 17, 2026 deadline). The next window is not announced.
who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.

name: Milpitas Youth Advisory Commission
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)

who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.

name: Mission College High School Dual Enrollment

how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.

name: City of Mountain View Teen Volunteer Summer Program
org: City of Mountain View, The View Teen Center

who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.

notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who represent Mountain View teens. The committee has fifteen members plus members-at-large. Residency or school rules are not spelled out on the page.

name: Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy (MTC)
