deadline_text: The 2026 program is over. The 2026 call was announced March 24, 2026; exact open and close dates are not on the page. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: Bay Area residents who attend a local high school, are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade before it starts. Parent or guardian permission is needed under 18. GPA is not considered.
how_to_apply: Contact Academy@BayAreaMetro.Gov or 415-778-5207. The page does not detail the application steps.
notes: MTC's older 'High School Internship Program' pages date to 2018; the high school program MTC lists now is this Academy. It is mostly virtual evening sessions, not a job placement.

name: NASA Citizen Science Projects
pay_detail: Free
duration: Whenever you want
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.

name: NASA GeneLab for High Schools (GL4HS)
city: Virtual (hosted by NASA Ames, Mountain View, CA)
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (and college freshmen)
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.
duration: 12 weeks, June 1 to Aug 28 in 2026
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026, or until 1,000 applicants. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.

name: Newport Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are first-come, first-served and accepted as needed.
who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.
how_to_apply: Teens fill out the online application themselves on the library's volunteer portal (application form number 2) and lead communication with staff. You must attend volunteer training before starting.
notes: Volunteers age 15 and up must complete fingerprinting and a background check. Applying does not guarantee a spot. Questions go to the library's Teen Services team through the email link on the page.

name: Newport Beach Teen Leader Program
org: City of Newport Beach Recreation and Senior Services
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Thursday, May 1, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.

name: Marine Teens Internship
org: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (NHMLAC)
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the application link and deadline.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the program page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.

name: NOVAworks Young Adult Services
city: Sunnyvale, CA (serves San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County)
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
deadline_text: Open enrollment. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale. High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income plus justice involvement, unstable housing or foster care.
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. Most applicants need a documented barrier and income under the program limits.

name: National Park Service Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
city: Participating national parks (see the NPS park list)
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 season open in late January or early February 2027. Closing dates are set by each park and are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.

name: Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
deadline_text: Submit your materials before Dec 4, 2026 to be invited to an interview. No final deadline is posted. Info session Sat Oct 17, 2026, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who start in Tier 1 (9th grade), Tier 2 (10th grade or Tier 1 done) or Tier 3 (11th grade or Tier 2 done). No age or borough rule is stated. You do not have to share immigration status for Tiers 1 to 3.
how_to_apply: Apply online (account lets you save progress): short answers plus references, then a group interview. Apprentices must reapply every year. Two references use a separate online reference form.
notes: Tiers 1 to 3 are not employees. Tier 4 apprentices must be legally authorized to work and eligible under NYC Department of Labor rules, per the program page. Partial participation is not allowed. Questions: gap@bbg.org (shown on the page) or 718-623-7252.

name: Pre-College Programs: NYC Commuter Summer
org: Columbia University School of Professional Studies
grades: Entering grades 9 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: 1-week session $2,883. 3-week session $6,381. Plus an $95 application fee and $50 or more for course materials. Deposit $1,000 (1-week) or $2,000 (3-week) is credited toward the cost. These are estimates pending trustee approval.
duration: 1 week (Jun 21 to 25, 2027) or 3 weeks (Jun 28 to Jul 16, 2027; more sessions listed on the dates page).
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open mid-November 2026. Early registration deadline Feb 1, 2027. General application deadline Apr 1, 2027 for the NYC Commuter sessions.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 or freshman year of college. The commuter option is for students who live in or near NYC. Academic strength is what the admissions team looks for.
how_to_apply: Online application. Columbia says applications are reviewed on the dates-and-deadlines schedule; early registration is cheaper to plan around.
notes: Expensive; the page says financial aid details are elsewhere and they were not read. The commuter page still shows a $95 application fee under a Summer 2026 cost heading while the cost page for Summer 2027 says $80. Free Columbia programs for NYC teens (Double Discovery Center, Freedom and Citizenship) exist but their pages blocked access, so they are not listed.

name: Summer Innovation Intensives
grades: Finished sophomore year of high school or later
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page (students earn 2 Cornell credits). Ask summer@tech.cornell.edu before applying.
duration: 3 weeks, commuter only (no housing). Exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program page.
deadline_text: The summer 2027 application will open in winter 2026. The summer 2026 application is closed. No deadline posted. Rolling review.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 19 who completed 10th grade by the program start, live in the NYC area (or arrange a supervising adult and housing), and are U.S. citizens or permanent residents at U.S. curriculum schools. No interview or minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript, two recommendation letters and short essays (250 to 300 words each). Contact: summer@tech.cornell.edu.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page read, so confirm the price and any financial aid with the program before applying. Selective. International students are not admitted at this time.

name: Ladders for Leaders
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
grades: Rising high school seniors and college students
pay_detail: At least $16.50 per hour in 2025 (2025 FAQ). 2026 pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 6 weeks, 25 to 40 hours a week (2025 FAQ)
deadline_text: DYCD page says the deadline for the last cycle was extended to January 16, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: 2025 FAQ: rising high school seniors or college students ages 16 to 24 who can legally work in the U.S. and have some prior paid or volunteer work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the SYEP application online at application.nycsyep.com and choose a Ladders community partner. Selection uses a personal statement, transcript and resume, then workshops, mock interviews and employer interviews (2025 FAQ).
notes: Competitive. Eligibility, pay and process come from the 2025 FAQ because no newer FAQ was found, so check the DYCD page when applications reopen. Interns under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). Free to apply.

name: Learn & Earn
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
pay_detail: Paid six-week summer internship. Rate not stated on the page.
duration: Year-round program with a six-week paid summer internship
deadline_text: Page says enrollment dates are September 1 to 30 (year not stated). That window has passed for this fall.
who_can_apply: NYC high school juniors and seniors who live in New York City, are low income (or meet an exception such as public assistance, foster care or living in a high-poverty area) and meet at least one other listed need. The page lists age 16 to 21 in one place and 14 to 21 in another, so ask a provider.
how_to_apply: Contact a Learn & Earn provider from the DYCD list, or call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646. Providers check your eligibility.
notes: Income-based, with extra eligibility rules listed on the page. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
pay_detail: Ages 16-24 (2026): $17.00 per hour, 25 hours a week. Ages 14-15 (2026): up to $700 for about 12.5 hours a week.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed March 13, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who live in the five boroughs of NYC and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. Some options (school-based, NYCHA, foster care, homeless youth) have extra rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at application.nycsyep.com or on paper with an SYEP provider. One application only. Community-based placements are picked by random lottery. Have ID documents ready (proof of age, identity, address, Social Security).
notes: Pay and hours above are the 2026 numbers and may change. Free to apply. NYS Department of Labor says anyone 14-17 needs working papers (employment certificate) to hold a job in New York State; ask your SYEP provider what they need from you. Teens in school-based (CareerReady) options apply through their school. You pay your own transportation and meals.

name: Work, Learn & Grow (WLG)
org: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD)
pay_detail: New York State minimum wage, paid every two weeks (DYCD FAQ).
duration: 22 weeks, Oct 26, 2026 to Apr 3, 2027, 250 hours total
deadline_text: The WLG application page lists a deadline of October 9, 2026. The FAQ PDF lists the application period as Sept 8 to Oct 2, 2026, so confirm with your SYEP provider.
who_can_apply: NYC residents legally allowed to work in the U.S. who took part in the 2026 Summer Youth Employment Program as CareerReady (ages 16 to 19 in a CareerReady partner high school) or in Special Initiatives (ages 16 to 20, in high school or a high school equivalency program), as of Oct 26, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the WLG online application (CareerReady or Special Initiatives link), or ask your SYEP provider for help. If selected, submit documents online or in person to your provider.
notes: Only for teens who were in 2026 SYEP through a partner school or Special Initiatives provider, so most teens cannot start here. Internet access is required. Closing today or very soon as of the verification date. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).

name: Summer Volunteer Program for High School Students
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Summer session runs June to September; minimum 100 hours; each session at least 3 to 4 hours.
deadline_text: The page still shows Summer 2025 postings with high school applications January 1 to May 31. No 2027 dates are posted. Onboarding takes about a month, so apply early in spring.
who_can_apply: Students 16 and older (some roles, such as Maternal Child Health, require 18). Montefiore also partners with SYEP; its SYEP provider is Children's Arts and Sciences Workshop.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Summer Volunteer - High School posting on Montefiore's career site (linked from the volunteer page), then attend an orientation and interview. Interviews are first come, first served.
notes: Confirm first: the dates are from the 2025 posting. Contact: volunteerservices@montefiore.org (shown on the page).

name: Junior Medical Program (JuMP) and high school volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no JuMP cost or pay.
duration: JuMP: 6 weeks, 100 hours. Unit Support: one 3-hour shift a week; the page lists a 100 hour minimum for high school students.
deadline_text: JuMP applications are accepted January 1 to March 1 (no year given on the page; expect Jan 1 to Mar 1, 2027). Space is limited. The process can take 4 to 8 weeks.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. JuMP is for ages 15 to 17 and requires full availability for all six weeks. Unit Support is open to high school students. The emergency department and some other roles are 18+.
how_to_apply: Online application, one letter of recommendation from a non-relative, and a resume.
notes: Read through the fetch tool because direct downloads were blocked. The page says volunteers need a valid Social Security number (a hospital clearance rule on the official site) and pay for their own medical clearance. Other Mount Sinai campuses have their own pages and age rules that were not read.

name: NYBG High School Explainer Program
pay_detail: Intern tier is unpaid volunteering (OMNY card help for transit can be provided). Later tiers (Advanced Explainer, Mentor, Senior) are paid part-time jobs; the page gives no hourly rate.
duration: Spring 2027 internship: one 4.5 hour Saturday or Sunday shift each week, Mar 20 to Jun 19, 2027 (minimum 105 service hours), plus 4 required training days (Mar 6, 7, 13, 14, 2027).
deadline_text: Spring 2027 application closes Saturday Nov 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Open House Sat Nov 7, 2026, 1 to 2 p.m. (RSVP by Oct 30). A fall session also runs; its applications open late spring.
who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12. The application form says weekday internship options are only for Partnership School students, so check which options you can apply for.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Complete applications get an invite to a group interview at the Children's Adventure Garden. Accepted teens attend orientation with a parent or guardian and 24 hours of training before starting.
notes: Questions: explainers@nybg.org. Intern tier is unpaid, so a work permit is not clearly needed there; the paid tiers are jobs and the page does not say what papers are required. The orientation date printed on the page shows the wrong year, so confirm it with NYBG. Late applications roll to the next session.

name: Summer Only Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Minimum 120 service hours over the summer.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted January 1 to March 31 (the page gives no year; expect Jan 1 to Mar 31, 2027).
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 (18 for some programs; check each campus). The Queens and Hudson Valley campuses do not offer Summer Only volunteering. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application and choose Summer Only plus your preferred program and campus. A volunteer services representative contacts you for an interview if a spot is open.
notes: Many NYP roles (emergency department, palliative care and others) are 18+. Brooklyn Methodist also runs a Junior Volunteer Program that was marked full when searched; its own page was not read for details. This entry covers the system-wide Summer Only option only.

name: Summer Volunteer Program, Manhattan Campus
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says no pay or school credit is given.
duration: 8 weeks, two 6-hour shifts a week (100 service hours total).
deadline_text: Applications open annually January 15 to February 15 (or until capacity is reached). The page gives no year; expect Jan 15 to Feb 15, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old at the start of the program. Under 18 cannot volunteer during the school year. The year-round program is 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Online application, a group information session, full summer availability, onboarding, health clearance (TB test, MMR and varicella proof, flu shot) and a background check.
notes: The Brooklyn campus requires age 18+. Long Island has its own teen program (not read in detail). The FAQ page still shows old 2022 dates, so only the Manhattan page was used for dates. Med-career internships and research are handled separately through HRNTV@NYULangone.org.

name: ARISE (Applied Research Innovations in Science and Engineering)
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (10th or 11th graders applying)
pay_detail: Free. A $2,000 stipend is paid for completing the program.
duration: 10 weeks: about 4 weeks of remote after-school workshops in June, then 6 weeks of in-person lab work (about 150 hours of lab experience). Summer 2026 ran Jun 1 to Aug 14, 2026.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 deadline was Feb 27, 2026 at 5 p.m. Summer 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Full-time NYC residents who attend NYC schools, applying as 10th or 11th graders (rising juniors and seniors), with strong grades and interest in STEM. Students from groups underrepresented in STEM are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Online application (optional recommendation due after), a group interview and lab tours to pick your placement.
notes: Selective with limited spaces. Funded by the Pinkerton Foundation. Students present at an AMNH poster symposium at the end. The two NYU pages differ slightly on grade wording (10th or 11th grade now versus rising juniors and seniors), which is the same group. The program name on a second page reads Applied Research In Science and Engineering.

name: Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
grades: Current high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: Free to apply and attend. An OMNY card covers NYC transit. Stipends are not guaranteed; need-based stipends may go to students with financial hardship who meet all attendance rules.
duration: 7 weeks, Mon Jun 21 to Thu Aug 5, 2027, full time (about 35 hours a week, roughly 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: Applications for SSRP 2027 open Oct 15, 2026. The deadline is not posted yet. The last cycle closed Fri Jan 2, 2026 (letters of recommendation due Jan 5), with Zoom interviews in March and decisions in April.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors or seniors who are at least 16 when the program starts. Students from outside NYC and outside the Tri-State area may apply but get no help with housing or travel. No GPA minimum. Sophomores are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a letter of recommendation and a transcript (to confirm you are in high school). Selected applicants get a Zoom interview.
notes: Very competitive (about 32 students a year). You must attend the entire program with no gaps. Minors cannot work with human patients. You may not use SSRP work in science competitions. The program page labels its glance box SSRP 2026 but lists the 2027 dates. Contact: program administrator listed on the page, 1230 York Ave.

name: Discovery Guide Youth Volunteer Program
org: Wildlife Conservation Society (Bronx Zoo, Central Park, Prospect Park and Queens Zoos, New York Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
deadline_text: Not accepting applications now. Applications for the next cycle open in late December 2026 for Spring 2027. No closing date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.

name: Youth Insights (YI Artists, Arts Careers, Introductions, Leaders)
grades: Grades 9 to 12 (varies by program; YI Leaders is grades 11 and 12)
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.
deadline_text: YI Artists (this semester) deadline was Sep 9, 2026 (extended). YI Arts Careers and YI Introductions list no 2026 deadline and reopen in Summer 2027. No YI Leaders deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: NYC high school students. YI Artists: grades 9 to 12. YI Arts Careers: entering grades 10 to 12. YI Introductions: entering grades 10 to 12 who are English Language Learners. YI Leaders: grades 11 to 12 who finished at least one semester of YI Artists or YI Arts Careers.
how_to_apply: Online form for each program (links on the Youth Insights page). YI Leaders is for teens who have already done another Youth Insights program.
notes: The page's closing note also lists YI Introductions graduates as eligible for Leaders, which conflicts with its Open to line. The page lists no program contact; use whitney.org/contact. The Whitney also runs a separate Open Studio for Teens (free).

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE) high schools
pay_detail: Part of the school day at no cost. Some work-based learning (such as apprenticeships) can be paid, but pay is not stated on this page.
duration: Grades 9 to 12
deadline_text: Enroll through the regular NYC high school admissions process. Dates are not stated on the CTE page.
who_can_apply: NYC public high school students at one of the 130+ schools with CTE programs. Students who finish a state-approved program can earn a CTE endorsement on their diploma.
how_to_apply: Browse programs on NYC MySchools. Talk to your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center about admissions and enrollment.
notes: This is a school choice, not a job. Ask your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center how enrollment works for your grade. The CTE endorsement needs 44 credits, 5 Regents exams, a technical assessment and work-based learning.

name: Career Readiness and Modern Youth Apprenticeship (CRMYA)
org: NYC Public Schools with CareerWise New York
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
deadline_text: Dates are not stated. Juniors apply during the school year; ask your school.
who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor.

name: Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP)
org: City of Oakland, Oakland Workforce Development Board, and partner nonprofits
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage; exact rate set by each partner
duration: Up to 100 paid hours (varies by partner)
deadline_text: Deadlines vary by partner. For Summer 2026 one partner (ACOE) closed recruitment June 18, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; check partner sites in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Must live in Oakland. No work experience needed. Free. Partner groups set their own ages (for example YEP 14 to 18, Youth UpRising 14 to 21, Lao Family 16 to 21).
how_to_apply: Pick a partner from the City list (YEP, Youth UpRising, Lao Family, Trybe, Rising Sun, Destiny Arts, Soccer Without Borders, YouthBeat, Alameda County Office of Education GCGI-GET) and apply on that group's site or by phone.
notes: City Council approved more than $3.1 million for 2026 and 2027 summer youth jobs, so a 2027 round is expected. Another City page lists ages 16 to 21, so check each partner's own age rule. Under-18 workers need a work permit (OUSD Linked Learning can help OUSD students).

name: Oakland Workforce Development Board Youth Summer Jobs (Lao Family, YEP, Trybe)
org: Oakland Workforce Development Board (City of Oakland)
pay_detail: Not stated on this page; the City's MSYEP page says at least Oakland's minimum wage
deadline_text: No dates posted. Contact the partners for the current cycle.
who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per this City page.
how_to_apply: Contact Lao Family Community Development (510) 533-8850, Youth Employment Partnership (510) 533-3447, or Trybe (510) 985-9915. OWDB email: OWDB@oaklandca.gov.
notes: This City page is older than the MSYEP page (which lists partners with other ages, such as YEP 14 to 18 and Lao Family 16 to 21). Treat 16 to 21 as the safe range and confirm with the partner.

name: Oakland Parks, Recreation and Youth Development (OPRYD) Part-Time Jobs
pay_detail: Not posted on the page; see each job posting
duration: Varies by posting; mostly seasonal
deadline_text: Deadline Oct 25, 2026 for Spring/Summer 2027 starts; Feb 7, 2027 for Summer 2027 starts; Aug 8, 2027 for Fall/Winter 2027 starts.
who_can_apply: Open recruitment for the City's recreation jobs; the page does not state a minimum age (lifeguards and many City jobs need 16 or older). Spanish, Cantonese and Mandarin skills are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Apply at governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca. Questions: parksandrec@oaklandca.gov, (510) 238-7275.
notes: The hiring process takes several months, so apply early. Check each posting for minimum age and pay. The governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca portal showed 0 openings on Oct 7, 2026, so if you cannot find the posting, call (510) 238-7275.

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
duration: One meeting a month
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Teens who join through the library teen volunteer application: ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. The TAB page itself states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and choose 'leadership', or ask your branch teen librarian.
notes: Meets monthly at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge. The same page also covers the Oakland Youth Poet Laureate program.

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Volunteer Program
duration: Shifts when the library is open; the form asks for morning and afternoon or evening availability, any day of the week
deadline_text: Rolling. Not every branch has space at all times.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. Also takes teens with court-ordered service hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application, or stop by a branch.
notes: The library cannot promise a spot at a specific branch. About two thirds of library volunteers are teens, per the page.

name: Teen Summer Internship (California Trail Interpretation)
pay_detail: $50 non-refundable fee when selected (aid available). No stipend is listed.
duration: About 200 hours over 7 weeks (June 10 to July 28 or Aug 1 in 2026); shifts 9 am to 4:30 pm, Sunday to Wednesday or Wednesday to Saturday
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade interested in animal care or environmental education.
how_to_apply: Online form with a cover letter (500 words max) and resume or transcript, then an interview.
notes: Up to 6 interns, so it is likely competitive. No stipend is listed; ask. Financial aid is available for the $50 fee.

name: Teen Wild Guides
pay_detail: $50 first year, then $25 a year; financial aid on request
duration: School year: every other weekend. Summer: about once a week. Shifts 9:30 am to 4 pm.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 info meetings Aug 15 and 16, applications due Sept 1, 2026, trainings Sept 26 and Oct 4. The page says applications are accepted year-round and later ones are reviewed in the next enrollment period.
who_can_apply: Must be 13 or turning 13 in the application season. Zoo page lists grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, interview, then attend both mandatory training days.
notes: Unpaid, and teens pay a small fee (aid available). Must be 13 or turn 13 in the application season.

name: ZooCamp Teen Assistant and Teen Interns
pay_detail: Teen Assistant unpaid (community service hours). Interns: $400 per week stipend, assuming full attendance.

notes: Great first step: be a Teen Assistant, then apply to be a paid intern. The 2026 info meetings were in March and the 2026 training was Sunday May 17; expect similar timing for 2027.

name: OC Fair & Event Center Jobs (annual OC Fair)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: The OC Fair runs for a few weeks in summer. Fairgrounds also hosts 150+ events a year.
deadline_text: No hiring dates posted on the jobs page for 2027.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 to work at the annual OC Fair. Some jobs require 18 or older. Applicants 17 and under must provide a valid work permit, available through their school, unless they have already graduated from high school. You must show documents proving identity and work eligibility in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Read the Fair's jobs page, then contact Human Resources at (714) 708-1563 or humanresources@ocfair.com. The page lists no application link.
notes: The page does not describe an application link or a pay rate, so call or email HR to ask when summer 2027 hiring opens. Applicants 18 and older must pass a background screening.

name: OC Public Libraries Teen Volunteer
city: Orange County, CA (any OC Public Libraries branch)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Flexible shifts, set by the branch
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings are limited and depend on each branch.

how_to_apply: Contact your local branch to confirm there is an opening. Once a spot is confirmed, fill out the OCCR Volunteer Registration Form, print it, and drop it off at the branch.
notes: The registration form is shared by several county agencies, so some questions may not apply to you. Ask your branch what it needs. Arrive on time and tell the branch as early as you can if you miss a shift. OC Public Libraries points teens who need court-ordered hours to the OneOC Court Referral Program.

name: OC Workforce Development Board READY S.E.T. OC (WIOA Young Adult Program)
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Wage not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Start by filling out the interest form.
who_can_apply: In-school young adults ages 14 to 21 who are low income (free or reduced-price lunch counts) and have at least one barrier: basic skills deficient or English learner, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school (adult education is allowed) and have a barrier such as dropout, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the READY S.E.T. OC interest form (Interest and Eligibility Assessment) linked on the page. Services are delivered by a network of regional providers, which the page does not name.
notes: Federal WIOA program, so eligibility rules apply (income and barriers). Cost to the student is not stated on the page. Questions: County Directory Assistance 855-886-5400. Many teens will not qualify, so read the eligibility list first.

name: OUSD Linked Learning Internships
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
fields: any; health; tech-cs; arts-media; engineering; business-finance

notes: The OUSD page still shows Summer 2024 forms, so look for a new form in January 2027. Not every internship is open to every student.

name: OUSD Linked Learning: Pathways, Internships and Work Permits
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)

name: Palo Alto Art Center Summer Camp Counselor in Training
org: City of Palo Alto Art Center
duration: At least 1 week

notes: Same page lists the Ceramics Apprentice Program (16 and older, 2 years of Art Center ceramics or instructor approval, 2 hours a week, one training session). Spots may fill fast once registration opens.

name: Teen Library Advisory Board (Palo Alto City Library)

deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in December 2026 to apply for Winter/Spring 2027.

notes: Fingerprinting is required. Log your hours in Better Impact or the library cannot confirm them.

name: Teen Advisory Board (Mitchell Park Teen Services)
org: City of Palo Alto, Mitchell Park Teen Services
deadline_text: The page mentions a deadline but gives no date or year. The only dates found were in a 2023 city article.

notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

name: Palo Alto Youth Council (PAYC)

notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

name: Pathful Explore (virtual career exploration)

notes: The home page names Pathful and Pathful Junior and does not use the name Pathful Explore. It is a school-run tool; individual students likely cannot join without a school plan.

name: Peralta Colleges Dual Enrollment (Laney, Merritt, Berkeley City, College of Alameda)

notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers including incoming 9th graders (2026 dates were June 22 to July 31; no application deadline posted). The old OUSD page mentions a stipend; the Peralta page does not.

name: Planting Justice Youth Internships

notes: Ages, season and hours are not stated, so call and ask. Pay is from the program page and may change.

The recruitment ad describes city commissions in general; the Youth Commission's own duties and term length were not on a page we could open, so what_you_do is based on the ad's general description.

name: San Mateo Police Cadet (Explorer) Program
duration: 9 week academy plus monthly service
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A recruiter contacts you after you send the application.

how_to_apply: Email the completed application to joinsmpd@cityofsanmateo.org or call the Recruiting Unit at 650-522-7629.
notes: Training classes are on the 1st and 3rd Thursday, 5 to 7 p.m. Hours count toward school service requirements. You need a flexible schedule for weekdays and weekends. FAQ is at cityofsanmateo.org/4720.

name: Hayward Police Explorer Program
deadline_text: Applications are taken twice a year, in January and July (page gives no exact dates). The next window is expected in January 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 (not yet 19 and a half), full-time student, 2.5 GPA, must pass a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, or contact the coordinator at 510-293-5060 or Explorers@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page gives no closing dates, so check at the start of each window. Meetings are Wednesday nights 5 to 7pm plus training and some weekend events.

name: Morgan Hill Police Explorer Program
pay_detail: Free; you may buy your own uniform (help available)
deadline_text: No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, currently enrolled in school with a C average or better. No felony or certain misdemeanor convictions, no pending criminal cases, and you must agree to fingerprinting for a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the Explorer application PDF to MHPD_Explorers@morganhill.ca.gov, then complete an oral board interview.
notes: Free to join, but you may need to buy a uniform and gear. Financial help is available. Expected to attend all meetings, trainings and events. Meeting times are not on the page.

name: Oakland Police Explorers
deadline_text: No intake dates posted. Contact the coordinator.
who_can_apply: High school students at least 14.5 years old, 2.0 GPA, average or better attendance and discipline, no felony or serious misdemeanor.

notes: The page gives a minimum age of 14.5 and no upper limit. The page does not give meeting times or dates, so ask the coordinator. Oakland PD also runs the Police Activities League.

name: Pretend City Children's Museum Volunteers and Teen Programs
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.

notes: Address: 29 Hubble, Irvine, CA 92618. Volunteer questions: volunteer@pretendcity.org or 949-428-3900. The page also links a Youth Leadership Board but does not describe it.

name: Peer-to-Peer Service Collective for Teens
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service credit for time presenting.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9-12 who live in the five boroughs, with parental consent and NYS working papers, and who register as library volunteers.
how_to_apply: Complete the Idea Submission questionnaire on the library volunteer site during a submission window. The Civic Engagement Team will contact you to get your idea library ready. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: A limited number of projects are accepted and a branch must agree to host. Other QPL pages list ages as 14-18 for this program, so check the age limit if you are 18.

name: Queens Public Library Teen Volunteering (ages 14-17)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours count as community service credit.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: Minors can apply year-round. Approval and placement can take up to 30 days, longer in summer and fall.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with a signed parent consent form. The page says some projects do not require NYS working papers, so check each project's description. Students at schools outside the country or the state may use a waiver.
how_to_apply: Get the parent consent form and NYS working papers (from your high school office), create a volunteer account, search projects and click Express Interest/Sign Up, then interview and get an offer letter. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: Library says some projects do not need working papers, so check each listing. Working papers take 1-3 weeks from your school, so start early. They are issued regardless of immigration status. Under-14s can only volunteer with a parent or guardian.

name: American Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care Training
pay_detail: Babysitting Basics Online costs $45 (4 hours, self-paced, certificate valid 2 years). In-person class prices vary by location.
duration: Online course: about 4 hours; in-person length varies
deadline_text: Ongoing.
who_can_apply: Red Cross says the in-person Babysitter's Training is for ages 11 to 16, and its online Babysitting Basics course is designed for youth 11 and older.
how_to_apply: Pick a class on the Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care page, or buy the online course there.
notes: The old take-a-class/babysitting-training link no longer works, so the page address was updated. Red Cross says these courses do not qualify you for state-licensed child care. Casual babysitting in a private home does not need a work permit per the California child labor guide (2013 edition).

name: American Red Cross Lifeguard and Water Safety Instructor courses
org: American Red Cross (taught by local pools, cities and YMCAs)

deadline_text: Ongoing. Class dates depend on the provider.
who_can_apply: Lifeguarding: at least 15 years old by the last day of class, plus a swim test (swim, tread water, timed event). Water Safety Instructor and Basic Swim Instructor: at least 15 by the end of the course.
how_to_apply: Use Find a Class on the Red Cross lifeguarding page to pick a pool or YMCA class near you, and check the fee.
notes: Final test is a 50-question exam with an 80% pass mark. Certificate lasts 2 years. Before the update this file said Water Safety Instructor needs age 16; the Red Cross page says 15. For lifeguard jobs, check each employer's page for pay and work permit rules.

name: Redwood City Leaders in Training (L.I.T.)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15; you must be 13 by the first training day. Written application, then an interview if selected. At most 20 L.I.T.s per session. Redwood City camps.
how_to_apply: Download the L.I.T. application and email it to tbrent@redwoodcity.org by the deadline. If chosen you interview, then get camp placement and payment instructions. Phone 650-780-5929.
notes: Teens pay a fee to take part (2026: $88, $98, $98 or $49 depending on session). The fee is due after a successful interview. Placement depends on camp needs. A mandatory Saturday training is required. 2027 dates are not posted, so expect a similar April to May window and watch the page.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the pages read; more than $7 million in awards and prizes
duration: May 2027
deadline_text: ISEF is in Los Angeles in May 2027 (exact dates not posted on the pages read). Affiliated fairs end by mid-April, and each fair sets its own deadline, so find yours now.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 or equivalent. You cannot enter ISEF directly; you must win at a Society-affiliated fair. Use the Find-a-Fair tool for California fairs.
how_to_apply: Use Find-a-Fair on the Society for Science site, then register with your school or regional fair.
notes: Projects can include no more than 12 months of continuous research. The 2027 ISEF is in California, which can lower travel costs for California finalists.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search

who_can_apply: Students in their last year of high school who live and attend school in the US or its territories, any citizenship. You need your own original research with real data, plus essays, a paper of up to 20 pages, recommendations and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Society for Science application portal (sciencetalentsearch.smapply.org).
notes: Seniors only, so juniors should plan for next fall. Test scores are optional. Homeschooled students may apply.

name: Richmond YouthWORKS Work Experience Program (WEX)

name: Climate Careers (Green House Calls)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up. Spots are limited and not every applicant is chosen.
how_to_apply: Send the interest application and a letter of recommendation to Megan Eaton, meaton@roseville.ca.us, by the deadline. Selected applicants are interviewed, placed at a program site, then pay the course fee.
notes: The page does not say what day applications opened, only the May 5, 2027 deadline. You pay the course fee only after you are chosen. A separate LDP information sheet is linked on the page.

name: Volunteer at the Roseville Public Library

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)

pay_detail: Free to students

how_to_apply: Apply on the CEE site: essays, two or three teacher recommendations, official transcript, and PSAT, SAT, ACT or AP scores.
notes: Extremely selective (the FAQ says under 2.5% are accepted). Held in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so plan for travel. The older FAQ page mentions a $75 application fee with waivers and a minimum age of 16 by July 1, but it also lists a six-week program, so it may be out of date. Confirm with CEE.

Pay and ages for each cohort are not stated.

name: Youth volunteers at Sacramento animal shelter

notes: Fall sessions are at Evelyn Moore (Mon and Wed) and Clunie (Tue and Thu) Community Centers, 4:30 to 7:00 pm. You must be 13 on the first day. Only one absence is allowed. Graduated high school seniors who are in college do not qualify.

name: Teen volunteers at Sacramento Public Library
deadline_text: Rolling. The library says processing takes about a month and placement can take 2 to 3 months.
who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. A parent or guardian must sign the application before you start. The page does not state ages; ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Teens who need school hours can ask about drop-in volunteering at a branch.
notes: Many people apply, so a spot is not guaranteed. Drop-in is the quickest way to start; scheduled volunteering needs a longer onboarding. Court-ordered hours are not accepted.

name: Summer Youth Academies
org: Sacramento State College of Continuing Education
pay_detail: Estimated cost $205 to $520 per academy.
duration: 1 week each (2026: June 22 to July 31)
deadline_text: The 2027 schedule is posted in January 2027. Online registration opens Monday, March 1, 2027. No closing date stated.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12. Academies are sorted into 7th to 10th and 9th to 12th grade groups.
how_to_apply: Choose an academy once the 2027 schedule is posted, then register online starting March 1, 2027.
notes: Offerings change each year; the page lists 2026 courses as examples. Some academies are online and some are in person, and the same course may have an online and an in-person section. Open to students entering grades 7 to 12.

name: Summer @ City Hall
org: City of Sacramento Youth, Parks and Community Enrichment with SCUSD, Twin Rivers and Natomas USD
pay_detail: $500 stipend plus 5 high school elective credits (letter of completion for other schools).
duration: 6 weeks (2027 start June 14)
deadline_text: Application opens Apr 1, 2027 and closes Apr 12, 2027. Interviews start Apr 19, orientation May 22, program starts June 14, 2027. Dates are tentative.
who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who attend a Sacramento City, Twin Rivers or Natomas high school or live in Sacramento city limits.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the program page when the window opens. Email summeratcityhall@cityofsacramento.org with questions.
notes: Dates are tentative. The city also runs Semester @ City Hall, a 6-week spring and fall version open to any high school student who lives or goes to school in Sacramento city limits; its dates are not posted yet.

name: Sacramento Youth Commission
pay_detail: $50 per meeting attended, according to the FAQ.
duration: 2-year term (up to 2 terms in a row). Up to 10 hours a month. Meets the 1st Monday of the month, 5:30 to 7:30 pm, in person.
deadline_text: Apply when a seat is open. No dates posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 22 at the time of appointment. You must live in Sacramento city limits or go to school there for your whole term. City employees cannot serve.
how_to_apply: Apply online for an open seat. The city clerk reviews it, then there is an orientation and a supplemental application. The Mayor nominates and the City Council approves.
notes: Appointed by the Mayor and City Council, so not every applicant is picked. The FAQ says the $50 stipend applies to the 1st and 3rd monthly meetings. No experience needed. Seats open at different times; check the Become a Commissioner page.

name: Zoo Teens
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: $30 uniform fee.
duration: Jan to April 2027. 3-hour weekend shifts, at least 2 shifts (6 hours) per month
deadline_text: Applications open online Oct 10, 2026 for Zoo Teens 2027 (Jan to April). Closing date not stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, 2.75 GPA (proof needed), letter of recommendation, interview, $30 uniform fee, mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online starting Oct 10, send a recommendation letter and proof of GPA, then interview with the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027. The Summer Camp Counselor teen role (ages 15 to 19) is closed for 2026; check back next year. Animal Care Volunteers must be 18 or older.

name: Sacramento Food Bank and Family Services: Volunteer
duration: Shifts of a few hours
deadline_text: Online calendar with open shifts.
who_can_apply: Age 10 and up. Ages 10 to 15 need an adult chaperone; ages 16 to 17 need parent permission (waiver emailed after sign-up).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a shift on the online calendar; groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org. Phone 916-456-1980.
notes: Closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot are required. Full shifts do not appear on the calendar, so check back. People who received food bank services in the past 12 months cannot volunteer there. Groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org.

name: Sacramento County fire explorer, academy and high school fire pathways list
deadline_text: Varies by program. Spring 2027 for the Sacramento academy and Cosumnes Explorers.
who_can_apply: The page says programs are typically ages 14 to 20 and often need a 2.0 GPA, high school enrollment and parent consent under 18. Each program has its own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the links on the Metro Fire page and contact each program directly.
notes: Details from the programs' own pages: Sacramento Firefighter Youth Academy is free, ages 14 to 17, 9 months of Saturdays 8 am to 2 pm starting end of July, 35 spots, applications open in spring. Cosumnes Fire Explorers are ages 15 to 18 (juniors and seniors), 2.0 GPA, and applications for next school year open in spring 2027.

name: Sacramento SPCA Youth Service Projects
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Regular volunteers must be 18. Students and scouts can do community service projects without direct animal care. The page states no youth age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Community Service Application, or take the online New Volunteer Orientation. Questions: rmaier@sspca.org, 916-504-2807.
notes: You can become a regular volunteer at 18. Court-ordered hours are not offered. You will not get a confirmation after you send the application; you may start a project any time.

name: Sacramento Works for Youth (WIOA)
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one service. Wage not posted on the page.
deadline_text: Recruitment is year-round.
who_can_apply: Sacramento County youth ages 16 to 24. Federal eligibility rules apply, so ask a Job Center whether you qualify.
how_to_apply: Visit a Sacramento Works Job Center (find one on the Sacramento Works site). Staff at each center help youth access services.
notes: Designed for youth with extra barriers. Work experience is one of several services in a case-managed plan, not an open job board. Ages 16 to 24 are served, so this is mostly for older teens.

name: Sacramento Youth Center job training and volunteering
pay_detail: Not stated. Ask the center whether classes cost anything and whether job training pays.
deadline_text: No application deadline. Classes have their own start dates (for example Robotics Oct 3 and Sewing Oct 16; the page shows no year).
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. The page gives no other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Register buttons on the Programs page, call 916-248-1081, or use the contact form.
notes: Open Mon to Sat, 12 to 6 pm, at 1901 Del Paso Blvd. The Cafe Paso job training cafe is marked temporarily closed, so ask whether job training spots are open. Pay is not stated.

name: SPARK Summer Youth Employment Program (San Bernardino County)
org: County of San Bernardino Human Resources
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour in 2026 (about 28 hours a week).
duration: 2026: about six weeks, June 15 to July 24, Monday to Friday
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened March 16 and closed at the first 800 applications or March 27, whichever came first. 2025 applications opened March 15. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: San Bernardino County residents ages 16 to 24 by the start date, legally authorized to work in the U.S., with a valid California ID card. Under 18 needs an approved work permit before day one.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the county's job site when the window opens in March, upload proof of age and residency, attend orientation, then get matched to a job.
notes: Very fast: the 2026 posting closed after 800 applications. Check hr.sbcounty.gov/spark-syep/ in early March 2027 and have proof of age, residency and a California ID ready. The county page shows a PDF on how to apply.

name: San Bernardino County WIOA Youth Programs (Youth Forward)
org: San Bernardino County Workforce Development Board
pay_detail: Work experience is one of the services. Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Varies by provider
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings depend on each provider's capacity, so call the provider that serves your city.
who_can_apply: Eligible youth ages 16 to 24. Specific eligibility rules are given by each provider.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the county's youth page. Openings depend on each provider's capacity.
notes: This is the year-round option when the summer SPARK program is closed. Phone numbers for each provider are on the county page. The page does not say whether 16 and 17 year olds are paid, so ask the provider about work permits.

name: San Diego Workforce Partnership youth career services
pay_detail: Services are free. Some opportunities include paid training or paid on-the-job work experience; rates are not stated.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline. The online application takes about 10 to 15 minutes, then staff contact you about next steps.
who_can_apply: Free career centers. The page says it has helped thousands of 16 to 24 year olds and states no eligibility age, so ask.
how_to_apply: Complete the online program application (10 to 15 minutes). The team follows up about next steps.
notes: The programs page also lists GenAI, workforce support for in-school youth across San Diego County school systems, and EXCEL for in-school and out-of-school young adults in the South Bay; their ages and dates were not checked. Pay and permit rules for under-18 placements are not stated.

name: San Jose Middle College (San Jose City College)
org: San Jose Unified School District with San Jose City College
pay_detail: Free college classes (6 to 9 college credits). The page does not state other costs.
duration: Junior and senior years (the page does not state a fixed length)
deadline_text: Not stated on the San Jose City College page. Ask the Middle College office for the application timeline.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors. The application needs an administrator recommendation, a teacher recommendation (core subjects), a parent questionnaire, a student questionnaire and an unofficial transcript, plus a 504 plan if applicable. The page does not say whether students outside San Jose Unified may apply.
how_to_apply: Deliver the application packet (administrator and teacher recommendations, parent and student questionnaires, unofficial transcript) to the Middle College office, Business Building B-107, San Jose City College. Questions: Lisa Canton, lcanton@sjusd.org, 408-298-2191 ext. 3996.
notes: Re-read the SJCC Middle College page on 2026-10-07. The SJUSD Middle College page it links to (https://www.sjusd.org/our-schools/middle-college/nav/) returns 404, so the district's application steps, deadline and selection rules could not be confirmed. Students are responsible for their own transportation. Students from SJUSD can still play sports and join clubs at their home high schools. Confirm the deadline and whether non-SJUSD students can apply with Lisa Canton before applying.

name: San Jose Public Library Teen Volunteers (Teens Reach, Book Reviewer)
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The page lists teen programs for ages 12 to 18. A minimum age for general volunteering is not stated. Sign up through the volunteer page and an orientation (on-site or virtual).
how_to_apply: Use "Sign Up to Volunteer" on the library volunteer page and the Better Impact system, and attend an orientation. Email volunteer@sjlibrary.org.
notes: Teen Book Reviewer roles are listed on Better Impact. See also the separate Teens Reach card. The Teens Reach card appears to describe the same program, and the age range differs between pages (12 vs 13), so confirm with the library.

name: San Jose Works
org: City of San Jose (work2future and Mayor's Gang Prevention Task Force)
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.
who_can_apply: San Jose residents. The paid work experience is for ages 14 to 18 who face barriers to employment. Job help (resumes, job fairs) is open to ages 16 to 29. Free to join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Youth Application on the San Jose Works page. A staff member contacts you afterward.
notes: Pay rate and placement dates are not posted on the pages I read. The paid work experience is for youth 14 to 18 with barriers to employment; placement is not guaranteed. The FAQ says job help is free for San Jose residents 16 to 29. Under 18 needs a work permit.

name: San Jose Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Council
duration: Two-year term
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council (open now): no deadline posted. Youth Commission (closed): recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth Advisory Council: ages 13 to 19 who live in a San Jose City Council district. Youth Commission: ages 14 to 20, must live in the district they represent, two-year term (up to two terms), meets 4th Monday at 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Fill out the District Youth Advisory Application for the YAC. A Youth Commissioner contacts you within about two weeks.
notes: Page is hosted by the library. Some council districts are unavailable or paused. YAC members earn community service hours. Pay not mentioned.

name: San Leandro Library Teen Volunteers
duration: At least 4 months
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in November 2026. Summer applications open in mid March, per the summer page.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who can commit to a regular weekly shift for at least 4 months. You must attend one orientation each school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online, attend an in-person orientation at the Main Library, sign the waiver, and commit to a regular shift. Returning volunteers must use their old MyImpact login.
notes: The page mentions both 2026 and January 2026 timing, so confirm the next cycle with the Teen Librarian. It also says a teen should handle their own emails, because the program is meant to prepare you for a first job.

name: San Leandro Youth Advisory Commission
org: City of San Leandro Recreation and Parks
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages or grades. Ask the Recreation office.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call Recreation at 510-577-3462 or email SLRec@SanLeandro.Org.
notes: Meets at 6 p.m. on the first Tuesday of the month at the Marina Community Center, 15301 Wicks Blvd. Events listed for the 2025-2026 term include the MLK Celebration and the Cherry Festival and Parade.

name: Jobs for Youth (County of San Mateo)
org: County of San Mateo Human Resources
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the pages I read.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.
who_can_apply: San Mateo County youth ages 14 to 21 can join. The county summer internship is only for members ages 18 to 21. You must attend a 1 hour job prep workshop before using the job board.
how_to_apply: Register as a student member on jobsforyouth.org, attend the 1 hour job prep workshop, then use the job board. For the internship you also attend a mandatory orientation.
notes: Teens under 18 can use the workshops and job board but not the county internship. Phone 650-599-7215, email jobsforyouth@smcgov.org. Must be a San Mateo County resident for the internship.

name: San Mateo County Libraries Teen Volunteers
duration: 6 months or 1 semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Minimum commitment 6 months or one semester. A free background check is required at 16 and older (takes 3 to 6 weeks).
how_to_apply: Pick a branch and apply for a role on Better Impact through the library volunteer page, or email volunteer@smcl.org.
notes: The page did not list a Teen Advisory Board. Roles are set by branch, and there may be a wait for an opening. Apply for your own branch (13 locations).

name: Santa Ana Zoo Volunteers (including Zoo Buddies)
org: Santa Ana Zoo (City of Santa Ana)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short-term: 40 hours or less (Greeter shifts Fri to Sun, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Long-term: more than 40 hours (shifts every day, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: No deadline. Long-term volunteers do an online and an in-person orientation offered every other month.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 12 years old with an adult, or 15 years old on their own. Zoo Buddies is for ages 12 to 14, who must volunteer with a parent or guardian age 18 or older, and both complete the requirements together.
how_to_apply: Long-term volunteers and Zoo Buddies apply with the online volunteer application on the zoo page. Short-term volunteers contact the zoo through its Contact Us page. The zoo does not accept walk-up volunteers.
notes: Short-term needs the City of Santa Ana one-time volunteer waiver. Long-term needs the city volunteer application, a TB test and a background check. The City of Santa Ana volunteer page says volunteers under 18 must complete a minor waiver form. The Santa Ana library teen volunteer program was not listed because the only page found was from 2021.

name: Santa Clara County Teen CERT Academy
pay_detail: Free
duration: 3 day academy (Friday evening to Sunday)
deadline_text: Join the waitlist for the next academy. The site shows January 8 to 10 with no year printed. The last academy was March 13 to 15, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who live in Santa Clara County.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the Teen CERT website or email scctcert@gmail.com. Paperwork drop-off happened before the last academy.
notes: The March 2026 flyer said ages 13 to 17 and the website says 13 to 18, so check your age with them. Cost is not stated; the last academy was at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Santa Clara County residents only.

name: Santa Clara Youth Commission
duration: September to May, up to six years
deadline_text: The 2026-27 recruitment is closed. The page does not give 2027-28 dates.
who_can_apply: Santa Clara residents ages 12 to 19. You cannot be employed by the City of Santa Clara.
how_to_apply: Apply during the yearly recruitment. Call the Youth and Teen Center at 408-615-3760 or email youthcommission@santaclaraca.gov to ask when it opens.
notes: Meets the second Tuesday of the month at 6 p.m. at the Youth and Teen Center, 2446 Cabrillo Ave. The page was last updated 2026-09-30.

name: County of Santa Clara Intern and Earn
org: County of Santa Clara Employment Connection
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week
duration: 8 weeks per cohort
deadline_text: Posted 2026 cohorts: Summer deadline May 20, program June 29 to Aug 7. Fall deadline Sept 19, program Oct 19 to Dec 11. The page also says it is accepting applications now; call to ask about the next cohort. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18 who get CalWORKs benefits, or current and former foster youth ages 16 to 24. Open to year-round employment services.
how_to_apply: Call 408-758-3797 to begin your application, or use the Register/Refer form on the page.
notes: Only for teens who get CalWORKs benefits or who are/were in foster care, so most teens do not qualify. Under 18 needs a work permit. Positions are across the county.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers (tutor a K-6 student)
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer page at sccld.org/volunteer or ask a local library.
notes: Serves the library district branches, not every city in the county (San Jose has its own library). Hours, training and schedule are on the volunteer page. See the separate homework-help tutor card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor) for a similar after-school tutoring role.

name: County of Santa Clara Student Internship Program (Level I, high school)
org: County of Santa Clara Employee Services Agency
grades: High school (regular, vocational or working toward equivalency)
pay_detail: Paid on a five-step county salary scale; the rate is not stated on the page (see the county salary plan).
deadline_text: No current posting for Level I. Subscribe to email alerts on the Student Intern, Level I job title or contact county departments. Applications are reviewed as departments ask and expire after 6 months.
who_can_apply: High school student (regular, alternative vocational, or working toward equivalency), enrolled or graduated within 6 months, legal right to work in the US, overall GPA of at least 2.5. Application plus transcript and proof of enrollment. Under 18 needs a work permit (from your counselor or EDD). May need Live Scan and a physical.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to alerts for the Student Intern Level I posting on the county jobs site and apply with your transcript when it opens. You can also email departments, or the coordinator at studentinterns@esa.sccgov.org.
notes: Interns can be hired any time of year depending on department needs, so keep the alert on. Some departments (District Attorney, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Parks) run their own internships; contact them directly.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor
city: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga, CA
duration: One semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older, free one afternoon Monday to Thursday from 3:30 to 6pm for a whole semester, and about 7 hours of training.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application on the library's volunteer page.
notes: The page lists these libraries: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga. Check that your branch is included. Training is online (about 7 hours). The broader card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers) also includes after-school tutoring of a kindergarten to grade 6 student.

name: Student Advisory Trustee, Schaumburg Township District Library
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: One year: October 2026 to September 2027
deadline_text: The 2026-27 term closed Aug 9, 2026. A new application period is likely in summer 2027 but has not been posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live within the Schaumburg Township District Library service area. Grade level is not stated.
how_to_apply: The page invites eligible teens to apply but does not describe the method. Watch the library's Student Trustees page or ask the Teen Department.
notes: Board meetings are the third Monday of each month at 6:00 p.m., plus monthly meetings with the Teen Department. The next-cycle timing is a guess from this year's August 9 deadline.

name: Sacramento County Office of Education Career Technical Education
deadline_text: Course catalog online; no student deadline posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Which classes you can take depends on your school district. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask your school counselor and look at the SCOE CTE course catalog. Contacts listed: Michelle McIntosh (Director), mmcintosh@scoe.net; Raelynn Sharp (Project Specialist), rsharp@scoe.net.
notes: The pages describe CTE (career technical education, 15 industry sectors) and list staff contacts. They do not list eligibility, enrollment steps, dates or work-based learning details. Treat this as a starting point and call SCOE. Age and grade are not stated, so ask your counselor.

name: Santa Clara Valley Medical Center Volunteers
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are accepted online year-round, and the office is looking for weekday morning or afternoon shifts.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must give one 4-hour shift a week for at least six months in a row and at least 100 hours. They cannot take summer-only or school-break-only volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a volunteer reference form, then interview, attend a 2-hour orientation, pass a background check and health screening.
notes: The health screening asks for proof of vaccines, a flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the last 3 months. Ask your parent to start gathering records early. Questions: vmcvolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org.

name: 826 Valencia Youth Programs
grades: Programs for ages 6 to 18; stipended roles for grades 8 to 12
pay_detail: Free programs; some leadership roles are stipended (amounts not posted)
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No dates posted. Check the 826 Valencia program calendar.
who_can_apply: Students ages 6 to 18. Many students join through partner schools; some workshops allow direct sign-up.
how_to_apply: Check the calendar on the 826 Valencia site or contact a Writing Center.
notes: All 826 Valencia programs are free, and most students join through partner schools. The stipended Youth Leadership Advisory Board (grades 8 to 12) and Black Literary Achievement Club are listed on the SFPL page; the stipend amount is not posted.

name: Breakthrough Leadership Program (BLP)
pay_detail: Paid through San Francisco's Opportunities for All program (rate not posted on the page). Some hours also count toward school volunteer requirements.
duration: Summer 2026 ran orientation June 15 to 18, then June 22 to July 31, 2026, about 6 weeks
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says the summer 2027 application launches in early 2027; exact dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Any current high school student (grades 9 to 12). Preference goes to current Breakthrough students and current or former Breakthrough volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill in the notify form on the BLP page to hear when the summer 2027 application opens.
notes: Breakthrough's separate Teaching Fellow job is a paid summer teaching residency with housing for people from outside SF and does not say it is for high schoolers, so it is not listed here. Located at 350 Masonic Ave.

name: Careers in Science (CiS) Intern Program
pay_detail: Paid above minimum wage (rate not posted)
duration: 2 to 3 years through graduation
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027; closing date not posted.
who_can_apply: Current 9th or 10th graders at an SFUSD school, with a 2.5 GPA and a C or higher in science and math, authorized to work in the US, able to commit 2 to 3 years through high school, and able to get to the Academy after school and on Saturdays.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in February 2027. Contact CiS@calacademy.org.
notes: SFUSD students only. Sign up for the Academy's Youth Programs mailing list to hear when applications open. Questions: CiS@calacademy.org.

name: CCSF Dual Enrollment (free college classes)
org: City College of San Francisco and SFUSD
pay_detail: Free
duration: By semester
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Ask your counselor before each term.
who_can_apply: SFUSD high school students, through a partnership with City College. Talk to your high school counselor about which classes are offered. Non-SFUSD students, or SFUSD students who want a class their school does not offer, use the Concurrent Enrollment page.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: dualenrollment@ccsf.edu. Non-SFUSD students use the CCSF Concurrent Enrollment page.
notes: Classes can be at your high school or at a CCSF location. A permission consent form for high school students is linked on the page. Grade and credit rules are not stated on the page, so ask your counselor.

name: Community Youth Center Youth Job Fair
org: Community Youth Center of San Francisco
pay_detail: Free event
duration: Wed Oct 14, 2026, 12 to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00 to 4:00 p.m. at Stonestown Galleria.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. Register with the Google Form on the DCYF listing.
how_to_apply: Register using the form linked from the sf.gov youth opportunities page. Bring a resume if you have one.
notes: The page does not list which employers will attend. It is a free event, not a job offer.

name: High School Elections Ambassador Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Ambassadors get a participation certificate signed by the Mayor and community service hours.
duration: About 2 weeks: Sept 14 to 27 in fall 2026, plus a 90 minute in-person training
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed (the round ran Sept 14 to 27, 2026). The program runs twice a year, in April and September. Spring 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students. No prior experience needed.
how_to_apply: Watch the Department of Elections high school programs page for the next application. Questions: hsp@sfgov.org or 415-558-6100.
notes: Same page: if you will be 16 by the next Election Day you can apply to be a high school poll worker, with a stipend up to $245. A poll worker application for the November 2026 election was due to be posted there in mid-August.

name: High School Explainer Program
pay_detail: Paid job; the wage is not on the program page
duration: A summer session or a school-year session, with over 60 hours of training (20 before working with visitors)
deadline_text: School-year applications are typically posted in July and summer applications in March. Closing dates are not stated.
who_can_apply: High school age students, 15 to 18 for first-time Explainers (up to 20 for returning ones). Must be able to get a work permit, attend all training dates and work the whole school year or summer session. No science background needed.
how_to_apply: When open, apply on the Exploratorium Current Openings page under the job title High School Explainer. Questions: hsesupervisors@exploratorium.edu.
notes: About 130 paid positions a year across two cohorts. The Current Openings list did not show on my read, so check it for a live posting. A separate PACE program serves ages 17 to 21.

name: San Francisco Fire Youth Academy
pay_detail: Free to join. Cadets get breakfast, lunch and a bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Saturdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., following the SFUSD calendar. A 2025 news article said 15 weeks each fall.
deadline_text: Not stated on the academy's site. A 2025 news article reported an Aug 11, 2025 deadline for the fall class.
who_can_apply: Cadets must attend high school in San Francisco (or equivalent) or live in the City and County of San Francisco. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the academy's website.
notes: The site does not list an age range or application dates, so ask the academy. Because it pays a stipend, ask whether a work permit is needed. It is a project of the SF Black Firefighters Association.

name: Girls on the Run Bay Area Junior Coach
org: Girls on the Run Bay Area
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 8 to 10 weeks, 1.5 to 3 hours per week; season starts early September, 5K on Nov 14, 2026

name: Summer VolunTEEN Program
